items.title: EPL: De Zerbi hails ‘complete’ Spurs after historic win at Chelsea
items.description: Roberto De Zerbi said Tottenham’s historic 2-0 victory against London rivals Chelsea proved his side have a winning mentality as they banished their dismal start to the season. Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League for just the second time in 36 years and the first since 2018. Trips across the capital to west London have largely been fruitless experiences for Tottenham over the last four decades. But De Zerbi’s men enjoyed a memorable visit to the Bridge on Saturday thanks to a comical own goal from Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders and a late wonder-goal from Mathys Tel after Blues star Cole Palmer was sent off. “It was a big moment for the fans, the club and the players also. They deserved this win, they prepared very well,” De Zerbi said. “We are improving a lot, we are improving in the mentality, in the group and the relationships with the players and then we are improving on the pitch.” Tottenham started the season on a dismal run of six league games without a win, raising the spectre of another relegation battle after they narrowly avoided dropping into the Championship on the final day of last season. With the pressure mounting on De Zerbi, the Italian has drawn his players closer together thanks to meals together and a trip to Marbella. – ‘The spirit, the belief’ – A win against promoted Coventry on Monday lifted the tension around the north London club and vanquishing Chelsea was another reward for De Zerbi’s team-building ethos. “Now it is a complete team. When we stay for dinner and stay together in the dressing room I see a different group, a different relationship and different atmosphere among the players,” he said. “The character was today great but we have many, many new players. The players who stayed here last season, two or three seasons ago, they suffered the last results, two times 17th position, we are working to change the last part of the history of the club.” Tottenham were beginning to lose the faith of their long-suffering fans after another miserable start to the season. But De Zerbi was adamant he never doubted they would get back on track. “I have to believe for sure in this group. I never lost the confidence in my players,” he said. “The week in Marbella, to speak better face to face, to open ourselves and remove the mask it is important. “It is important for the spirit, the belief. The atmosphere inside the dressing room is maybe more important than the tactics.” For Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso, it was a painful setback as the optimism engendered by successive victories over Bournemouth and Everton was washed away on a rain-lashed evening. Alonso’s expensively assembled team sit in fourth place but remain very much a work in progress after the third league loss of his first season in charge. “We are all disappointed with the result, with the performance collectively and individually we were not at our best level,” he said. “It was about the first goal and it went their way and with 10 men it was difficult but we can do better.” Alonso refused to blame Penders and Palmer for their roles in the defeat. “We feel for everyone, it is a team thing, a collective. We have to move on,” he said before adding he “hadn’t seen” Palmer’s two bookings. The post EPL: De Zerbi hails ‘complete’ Spurs after historic win at Chelsea appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Northern power brokers, Emirs, Imams behind Tinubu, Yari assures
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the power brokers of Northern Nigeria, traditional rulers and Islamic clerics are solidly behind his return to office in 2027. He spoke at the flag-off of the party’s presidential campaign in Kaduna, in the presence of the President and all the governors of Northern Nigeria. “We have been engaging all and sundry, our traditional rulers, our ulama and our imams, to understand the importance of your return in 2027 for continuity, for the peace of this country and for Nigeria,” Yari said. He told the President that the northern establishment had turned out in full. “We believe in you, and those people believe in us. All the shakers and movers of this part of the country are here. In the northern part of the country, anybody who is not here today, Mr President, then there is nobody there. We are here. “By God’s grace, Your Excellency, Mr President, we resolve, by God’s grace, that as far as Northern Nigeria is concerned, Mr President, I need your ears. Mr President, I want you to listen to us carefully. Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent for you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, by God’s grace, Insha Allah. And the promise we have made, you are going to see it on January 16, 2027,” Yari said. Yari described Kaduna as “the spiritual centre of politics in Northern Nigeria”, adding that the venue had drawn “all the governors of Northern Nigeria”. On the economy, he said the President’s reforms had changed the country’s fortunes. “If we talk about the economy, we know the state of the economy when you stepped into the leadership of this country. Today, the total indices have changed completely to the advantage of Nigeria and other countries of the world. “Mr President, I can enumerate at least a few: from the exchange rate, to the subsidy removal and many more,” Yari added. The APC-PCC boss said the party would take its case to voters on the strength of the administration’s achievements. “We Nigerians, at the head of this campaign, are going to campaign with our records. Our records are there. The infrastructure is there. What you did in health, education and human capital development is there. The students are there. The transparent cash and conditional cash transfers are also there for men and women,” he said. Turning to the 2023 election, Yari said: “I would like to be a student again, to be told how you did it, because we want the country.” He said the party was committed to justice and urged the President to listen closely to the North’s message. items.title: Nigeria, South Korea seek stronger trade, technology partnerships
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Nigeria and South Korea have called for stronger bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, technology transfer, agriculture and skills development to promote economic growth and create opportunities for their citizens. The two countries renewed the call at a reception to mark South Korea’s National Day in Abuja on Friday, with both sides expressing commitment to expanding their longstanding diplomatic relations. Speaking at the event, South Korea’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yoan, said the two countries, which established diplomatic relations in 1980, had opportunities to deepen economic cooperation through partnerships that support local businesses, entrepreneurship and human capital development. Jeong said South Korea was willing to share its development experience with Nigeria while respecting the country’s priorities and working with it as an equal partner. He recalled that South Korea’s economy was devastated by the Korean War, with its annual per capita income below $100 in 1953, but said investment in education, hard work and international cooperation had helped the country rebuild. The ambassador said the experience demonstrated the importance of investing in people, developing local industries and sustaining partnerships that deliver long-term benefits. Highlighting ongoing cooperation, he said the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), in partnership with Nigeria’s Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency (SMEDAN) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), broke ground on an entrepreneurship centre in Abuja in September. According to him, the centre is expected to support young entrepreneurs and start-ups by helping them develop business ideas and build sustainable enterprises. He also said South Korea’s Smart School project, implemented in collaboration with the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC), had reached about 8,000 children and provided training for more than 300 teachers and school leaders. Jeong added that KOICA and the Food and Agriculture Organisation were collaborating on an initiative to create green jobs for young Nigerians through agriculture. He said about 2,000 Nigerian officials had also received training in South Korea through KOICA programmes, describing capacity development as a key component of the bilateral relationship. On private sector cooperation, the ambassador identified opportunities for Korean companies to expand their engagement with Nigerian businesses in energy, manufacturing, clean water and digital technology. He listed Daewoo E&C, LG, Samsung, Hyundai and Solpia among Korean companies working with Nigerian partners, adding that the South Korean Embassy and the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) would continue to promote investment, technology sharing and local employment. Beyond economic and technical cooperation, Jeong highlighted the growing cultural relationship between the two countries, noting that Korean pop music, television dramas, films and beauty products had gained popularity among Nigerians. He said South Koreans had also shown interest in Nigeria’s Afrobeats music and Nollywood films, describing cultural exchanges as an important way of bringing the people of both countries closer. The ambassador said the theme of the celebration, “One Heaven. One Earth. One Humanity,” reflected the importance of peace, human dignity, mutual respect and international cooperation. He explained that South Korea’s National Foundation Day, known as Gaecheonjeol, is celebrated on October 3 and commemorates the country’s traditional founding story associated with Dangun and the principle of Hongik Ingan, commonly interpreted as “to benefit all humanity.” In her remarks, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, represented by the Chief of Protocol of the Ministry, Ambassador Babagana Wakil, commended South Korea’s achievements in technology, engineering, manufacturing and social development. She called for stronger cooperation in agriculture, industrial manufacturing, automobile assembly, shipbuilding and technology transfer, noting that closer collaboration could support Nigeria’s development priorities. The minister also identified education, digital technology, scholarships, technical training, academic exchanges and research as areas for expanded partnership between the two countries. She stressed the need to strengthen maritime cooperation in areas including maritime safety, transportation, fisheries and technical capacity development. Odumegwu-Ojukwu further called for renewed engagement under the Nigeria-South Korea Joint Commission framework to identify practical measures for increasing bilateral trade and investment. She said closer cooperation would enable both countries to address shared development challenges while creating more opportunities for their businesses and citizens. The reception featured a Taekwondo performance and Korean cuisine, showcasing aspects of South Korea’s cultural heritage. The event underscored the commitment of both countries to building on more than four decades of diplomatic relations through stronger economic partnerships, capacity development and cultural exchanges. items.title: Kaduna rally: Atiku challenges Tinubu over hunger, hardship
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain what his administration has done to end hunger and poverty, following the President’s claim that the opposition created the problems. Atiku said Nigerians were more concerned about the government’s record than its attempts to shift responsibility, insisting that the 2027 presidential election would put Tinubu’s handling of the economy and security under scrutiny. In a statement on Saturday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku accused the President of blaming his political opponents for hardship that had worsened under his watch. “Mr President, blaming the opposition for hunger is either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia. The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record,” Atiku said. On the economy, the ADC candidate challenged Tinubu to account for the consequences of petrol subsidy removal, the naira’s depreciation and rising poverty. “Which administration removed the petrol subsidy and watched the naira fall from about ₦471 to ₦1,329 to the dollar?” he asked. Atiku also questioned the government’s handling of public finances and the country’s poverty levels. “Which administration has presided over a rise in poverty that led the World Bank to estimate that 63 per cent of Nigerians will be below the national poverty line in 2026? Which administration extended the 2024 budget into 2025 while also operating a separate 2025 budget?” he asked. He further demanded explanations for what he described as questionable public spending, citing energy security expenditure, NNPC pipeline-related spending and charges associated with an Abu Dhabi financing facility. “Which administration recorded ₦7.13 trillion under ‘energy security’ in 2024 and faces questions over ₦11.2 trillion in NNPC pipeline related spending? Nigerians deserve to know who received these sums and what was delivered,” Atiku said. He also questioned the country’s external accounts and the charges associated with the financing facility. “Which administration must explain the $12.4 billion gap flagged in Nigeria’s external accounts for the first half of 2026? Which administration paid $22.5 million in ‘other charges’ on the Abu Dhabi financing facility?” he asked. On security, Atiku faulted the administration over persistent killings, kidnappings and displacement, demanding answers from the government. “Which administration is responsible for the killings, kidnappings and displacement that continue to terrorise communities? These are the questions Nigerians are asking while your government blames the opposition,” he said. Atiku also criticised Tinubu’s commissioning of the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium, arguing that the ceremony did not establish that the project had been completed. “Your decision to commission the unfinished Abuja to Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium shows how far removed you are from the daily reality of Nigerians. A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon-cutting ceremony,” he said. Returning to the central issue, Atiku said the government could not avoid accountability by blaming political opponents for describing the hardship Nigerians were experiencing. “You cannot govern for three years, make life harder, and then blame others for describing the hardship. You asked who created the hunger. Nigerians are asking what you have done to end it,” he said. He said the 2027 presidential election would test Tinubu’s record against the experiences of Nigerians. “The people will judge your government by the lives they are living, not by the excuses you offer at campaign rallies. “The 2027 presidential election will be a referendum on your record. Nigerians have felt the cost of your leadership in their homes, markets and communities. Their verdict is already clear: they have rejected your administration,” he added. Après avoir remporté le match retour sur le score de 1-0, l'Espétance est parvenue à s'imposer lors de la séance des tirs au but ce samedi 24 octobre au stade Hamadi Agrebi de Radès. Battus (0-1) lors de la manche aller à Misrata, les Sang et Or ont rapidement comblé leur retard dès la 9ᵉ minute grâce à une réalisation d'Imed Faraj,qui a ouvert le score mais malgré une nette domination et plusieurs occasions, l'Espérance n'est pas parvenue à inscrire le deuxième but libérateur durant le temps réglementaire. À l'issue des deux rencontres (1-1 au cumul des scores), la qualification s'est jouée lors de l'épreuve décisive des tirs au but. Le portier espérantiste Béchir Ben Saïd s’est alors illustré en stoppant deux tentatives adverse, propulsant ainsi le club de Tunid vers le tour suivant. L’Espérance de Tunis s'est ainsi imposée et qualifiée pour la phase de poules de la Ligue des Champions africaine. Y. N. items.title: Trump foreign policy hits voters in the pocketbook, imperilling Republicans in midterms
items.description: Foreign policy is rarely the deciding factor in US midterm elections, when economic considerations usually drive voters choices. But this time, with Donald Trump’s war on Iran and his sweeping tariff campaign pushing up costs for Americans, a presidents approach to world affairs has itself become a pocketbook issue. As the November 3 elections approach, there are growing signs that voters are drawing that connection directly, creating a major liability for Trump and his fellow Republicans and imperilling their control of Congress. A flag supporting US President Donald Trump outside the venue of his rally ahead of the midterm elections, in Macon, Georgia, the US on Oct 24, 2026. — Reuters Those include a Reuters/Ipsos poll earlier this month showing some 78 per cent of Americans blame Trump’s policies for rising prices that are outpacing their earnings. Not since 2006, when then-president George W Bush’s Republicans lost both legislative chambers while he was mired in the unpopular Iraq war, has a US leaders handling of international events appeared so central to shaping the midterms outcome. The political backlash for Trump could be even bigger, with opinion polls showing that voters feel the economic pain from high gas prices and rising grocery bills in a way that they didn’t two decades ago. The bottom line is people are experiencing the impact of Trump’s war and other policies, said Christopher Preble, a senior fellow at the Stimson Centre think tank in Washington. Now voters have a chance to register their discontent with how he’s dealing with all this. Politics driving foreign policy With Trump’s approval ratings touching historic lows , he has left little doubt, despite his public claims to the contrary, that he sees the straight line voters are drawing between his foreign policy and their cost of living. That has prompted some controversial policy moves in the run-up to the elections. Chief among them was Trump’s lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel exports aimed at bringing down fuel prices, a step his critics, including some fellow Republicans, say reinforces the impression that he is increasingly siding with Moscow in its war in Ukraine. He has also pressed Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian refineries as he tries to shift the blame for high US gasoline prices despite experts saying the surge in energy costs is mainly the result of the war he launched alongside Israel against Iran nearly eight months ago. Firefighters work at the site of an office building damaged during a Russian jet drone strike in Kharkiv, Ukraine on Oct 23, 2026. — Reuters At the same time, he has promised not to order any new attack on Iran before the midterms, though the US and Israel are widely reported to be preparing for a possible major escalation after the elections. Polls have shown that most voters oppose the war initiated by Trump, who had campaigned on avoiding new foreign interventions. He has insisted Americans should accept temporarily higher gas prices so that he can block Iran from developing a nuclear weapon. Iran says its nuclear programme is for civilian purposes. The UN nuclear watchdog and US intelligence community have assessed that Tehran shuttered a nuclear weapons development programme in 2003. Some Republican candidates have distanced themselves from Trump on matters ranging from the conflict in the Middle East to the trade war with Canada and his pressure campaign against Ukraine. For its part, Iran has sought to keep oil prices high and hurt Trump in the midterms by deploying new tactics to target ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and deliberately prolonging the diplomatic stalemate, senior Iranian officials have told Reuters. Defending the administration’s approach, White House spokesman Matt Middleton said: “President Trump has always been clear about temporary market disruptions as a result of the conflict in Iran, but the contrast between President Trump’s economic record and Democrats’ ruinous alternative is clear.” It’s the economy, stupid Midterm elections historically have been seen as a referendum on the performance of the incumbent in the White House. And in one election after another in recent decades, the conventional wisdom has been that economic concerns — it’s the economy, stupid, as the Clinton-era adage goes — dominate voters’ choices. Opinion polls for this year’s midterms, including the Reuters/Ipsos survey, show that while voters rank foreign policy low on their list of priorities, it is clear that most Americans see some of Trump’s signature moves on the world stage, such as the Iran war and tariffs, feeding into their higher costs. Footage released by IRIB and attributed to the IRGC shows oil tanker Gem No 2 ablaze, in this screengrab obtained from a video released on Oct 10, 2026. — Reuters/File Other polls have shown that a majority of Americans have also soured more broadly on Trump’s international approach. The Chicago Council on Global Affairs said its latest nationwide survey finds that most Americans believe the Trump administration’s foreign policy actions have negatively impacted America’s global standing and hurt national and household economic conditions. Since returning to the White House last year, Trump has shaken up the rules-based global order that Washington helped create from the ashes of World War Two while his relations with allies have steadily worsened and the limits of US power have been increasingly exposed, analysts say. Legislative balance of power in play Against this backdrop, Democrats are widely projected to gain control of the House of Representatives in the midterms, with the Senate also seen as increasingly in play. For Republicans, losing either chamber could complicate Trump’s agenda in the last two years of his second term. But even with a shift in the balance of power on Capitol Hill on Nov 3, lawmakers will have a hard time reining in Trump’s capacity to pursue foreign policy as he sees fit. Once the ballots are counted, a big question will be whether Trump will feel either restricted or emboldened on the world stage as he enters what is traditionally considered a lame-duck phase — when a president is barred from running again and no longer faces electoral consequences for decisions made. “For many presidents who feel politically constrained [at home], foreign policy is the area where they are able to act with relative freedom,” said Jon Alterman of the Centre for Strategic and International Studies think tank in Washington. Analysts say Trump’s handling of adversaries such as Iran, Russia, China and even Cuba or his approach to allies across the globe could go either way — or he could simply lose interest and double down on his string of construction projects, such as the White House ballroom.

items.title: Immobilier en Espagne : les Algériens premiers acheteurs étrangers à Alicante
items.description: Malgré une baisse globale des acquisitions par les étrangers, les Algériens demeurent parmi les nationalités qui achètent le plus de biens immobiliers en Espagne. Une région espagnole est particulièrement prisée des Algériens. Selon les chiffres du Portail des statistiques notariales, repris par le journal El Espanol, 62 327 transactions ont été enregistrées au profit d'acheteurs étrangers au cours du premier trimestre 2026, soit 13 % de moins qu’à la même période de 2025. La baisse a été de 9,7 % pour les résidents étrangers et de 18 % pour les non-résidents. Malgré le recul des ventes, les prix moyens du mètre carré des logements acquis par les étrangers ont continué d'augmenter, atteignant 2 644 €, soit une hausse de 9,4 % sur un an. Achats de logements en Espagne : les Algériens en tête à Alicante La région d’Alicante conserve sa position de principal pôle d'attraction de l'immobilier international en Espagne , avec 6 557 logements acquis par des étrangers au premier trimestre de l’année 2026. Dans la ville d’Alicante, où 584 logements ont été acquis par des étrangers au cours de la même période, ce sont les Algériens qui arrivent en tête avec 104 transactions. Malgré cette position, les Algériens ont nettement moins acheté dans cette ville qu'en 2025, où ils ont acquis 439 logements. Les Algériens sont suivis des Ukrainiens (62), des Italiens (47) des Néerlandais (27) des Polonais (25), des Français (25, des Roumains (23), des Allemands (21), des Russes (20) et des Britanniques (17). Malgré leur position à Alicante, les Algériens ne sont pas les premiers acheteurs dans toute l’Espagne. La première place revient aux Marocains, suivis des Britanniques, des Italiens, des Roumains et des Allemands. Les Algériens ont dépensé en moyenne 132 000 euros Les Marocains sont toutefois ceux qui acquièrent les biens les moins chers en Espagne. Les Algériens aussi ne figurent pas parmi les plus dépensiers. Les dépenses moyennes des acheteurs étrangers atteignent 245 431 euros. Les Néerlandais dépensent en moyenne 369 270 euros, viennent ensuite les Suisses (353 659 €), les Norvégiens (332 641 €) et les Belges (311 675 €). Les Algériens ont dépensé en moyenne 132 079 euros, loin derrière les acheteurs européens mais très largement devant les Marocains qui enregistrent la moyenne la plus basse par bien acquis, soit 53 257 euros. items.title: France : les gilets jaunes appellent à manifester le 31 octobre contre la «dérive autoritaire» du gouvernement
items.description: Les « gilets jaunes » ont appele, le 24 octobre, a une nouvelle mobilisation le 31 octobre pour denoncer ce qu'ils qualifient de « derive autoritaire » du gouvernement francais. L'annonce a ete faite lors d'une conference de presse place de la Bastille, a Paris, alors que plusieurs manifestations ont ete interdites ou soumises a des restrictions dans le pays. Le mouvement prevoit des rassemblements et des sit-in devant l'Assemblee nationale, a Paris, ainsi que devant les mairies a travers la France. Cette journee d'action vise a defendre les libertes publiques, notamment le droit de manifester. « Nous manifesterons pour la liberte de manifester, et pour toutes nos libertes », ont declare deux representants de sa coordination. Des restrictions qui alimentent la contestation Cet appel intervient une semaine apres les violences et les pillages du 17 octobre, dans un climat social marque par de nouvelles tensions. Le samedi 24 octobre, plusieurs corteges ont ete interdits ou ont vu leur itineraire modifie par les autorites. Des decisions vivement contestees par les organisateurs, qui y voient une atteinte au droit de manifester. a Paris, la prefecture de police a notamment interdit le parcours initialement prevu entre les places de la Bastille et de la Nation pour une manifestation contre la vie chere et en soutien aux revendications lyceennes. Un autre itineraire, entre la porte d'Italie et la porte de Vincennes, a ete impose. Les organisateurs ont finalement accepte ce changement apres le rejet de leur recours par la justice. Par ailleurs, les autorites francaises ont annonce la mobilisation de 70 000 policiers et gendarmes dans le pays pour encadrer les manifestations. Les gilets jaunes accusent le gouvernement de repression Face a ces restrictions, les representants des « gilets jaunes » denoncent la politique du gouvernement, qu'ils accusent de repondre aux revendications sociales par la repression plutot que par le dialogue. « Il y a une colere dans ce pays » qui « n'est pas entendue », ont-ils declare, denoncant le « mepris », le « refus d'ecouter », le « mensonge » et la « repression » de l'executif. Les organisateurs accusent egalement le gouvernement de chercher a affaiblir la contestation en divisant les manifestants. « Le gouvernement tente de nous diviser. En criminalisant notre mouvement, il veut empecher le front uni qui est en train de naître », ont affirme les representants du mouvement. En reponse, ils appellent a organiser des « assemblees de convergence » partout en France, afin de reunir lyceens, etudiants, travailleurs, paysans, retraites et « gilets jaunes » autour de revendications communes. « Notre reponse, c'est l'union », ont-ils insiste. La mobilisation du 31 octobre doit ainsi permettre au mouvement de defendre le droit de manifester et de federer les differentes composantes de la contestation sociale.

items.title: Le Sénégal s’engage pour un financement accru de l’évaluation des apprentissages
items.description: Représentant le chef de l’État lors de la présentation officielle des résultats du Programme d’analyse des systèmes éducatifs de la Confemen (Pasec 2024), hier à Dakar, le directeur de cabinet du président de la République, le Pr Mary Teuw Niane, a annoncé l’engagement de Bassirou Diomaye Faye à plaider pour un financement plus soutenu de l’évaluation des apprentissages. Il a mis en avant le rôle du programme dans l’amélioration des politiques éducatives et rappelé les réformes engagées au Sénégal. Le Sénégal entend faire de l’évaluation des apprentissages un instrument de souveraineté éducative et un levier de transformation de son système d’enseignement. Ce message a été porté, hier, à Dakar, par le directeur de cabinet du président de la République, le Pr Mary Teuw Niane, à l’occasion de la présentation officielle des résultats du Programme d’analyse des systèmes éducatifs de la Conférence des ministres de l’Éducation des États et gouvernements de la Francophonie (Pasec 2024). Représentant le chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, il a réaffirmé l’importance des données scientifiques dans la conduite des politiques publiques et annoncé un engagement présidentiel en faveur du financement des évaluations. « Une évaluation n’a de valeur que si ses données et ses analyses deviennent des décisions », a-t-il déclaré. Pour le Pr Mary Teuw Niane, le Pasec ne saurait se limiter à la production de statistiques sur les performances scolaires. Il doit permettre aux gouvernements de mieux cerner les difficultés rencontrées par les élèves et de mesurer les progrès accomplis. « Passer de la donnée à la décision, voilà ce que le Pasec rend possible », a-t-il insisté. Le représentant du chef de l’État a salué les efforts déployés depuis 1991 par la Confemen pour accompagner ses pays membres dans l’évaluation de leurs systèmes éducatifs. Il a également souligné le travail méthodique des équipes nationales. À ses yeux, l’expertise acquise au fil des années confère au programme une portée qui dépasse le seul cadre technique. « Il est fondamentalement un outil enraciné dans nos réalités politiques, sociales et pédagogiques, voire un outil de souveraineté éducative au service de décisions justes et éclairées », a-t-il affirmé. Cette reconnaissance s’accompagne d’un engagement au plus haut niveau de l’État sénégalais. Selon le Pr Mary Teuw Niane, le Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye soutiendra les initiatives destinées à renforcer le Pasec et à conforter sa place parmi les instruments de référence des systèmes éducatifs africains. Le chef de l’État a notamment accepté de porter auprès de ses pairs un plaidoyer en faveur d’un financement plus soutenu de l’évaluation des apprentissages. Le directeur de cabinet a précisé que ce plaidoyer serait défendu dans les instances régionales, notamment au sein de la Communauté économique des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (Cedeao). Il a également appelé l’Union africaine, les organisations sous-régionales et les partenaires au développement à soutenir davantage les politiques éducatives fondées sur des données probantes. L’éducation au cœur de Sénégal 2050 Évoquant les orientations nationales, le Pr Mary Teuw Niane a inscrit cette ambition dans l’Agenda national de transformation Sénégal 2050, dont le pilier consacré au capital humain et à la justice sociale fait de l’éducation et de la formation professionnelle des priorités. « Une société juste et prospère est une société qui investit sans relâche dans son capital humain », a-t-il soutenu. Il a estimé que le potentiel de la jeunesse africaine ne pourrait se traduire en développement qu’à travers des investissements judicieux dans les écoles et les centres de formation. « Ce dividende ne se décrète pas, il se construit », a-t-il résumé. Dans cette perspective, le représentant du chef de l’État a présenté plusieurs chantiers engagés par le gouvernement sénégalais. Il a cité la réécriture des curricula afin d’accorder une plus grande place aux mathématiques, aux sciences, aux technologies, au numérique et à l’intelligence artificielle. Il a également évoqué le renforcement de l’enseignement des langues nationales à travers le modèle harmonisé d’enseignement bilingue, dans le but de mieux ancrer les apprentissages dans les réalités linguistiques et culturelles du pays. Parmi les autres mesures mentionnées figurent l’initiative Nithé, lancée en janvier 2025, et la suppression du concours d’entrée en sixième, présentée comme un moyen de favoriser une continuité plus équitable du cycle fondamental. Le Pr Mary Teuw Niane est également revenu sur les assises nationales des daaras, destinées à moderniser l’enseignement coranique et à améliorer les perspectives d’insertion des talibés, ainsi que sur les réformes engagées dans l’enseignement supérieur, la recherche et l’innovation. Il a cité, en outre, la réforme du calendrier de versement des bourses universitaires et l’élargissement de l’offre de formation professionnelle et technique grâce à la création de nouveaux centres et instituts supérieurs. Ces initiatives doivent permettre aux jeunes, quel que soit leur lieu de résidence, d’accéder à des parcours de formation adaptés. « Voilà ce que signifie pour nous faire de l’éducation nationale une priorité, non pas un slogan, mais un engagement », a-t-il souligné. Le Pr Mary Teuw Niane a enfin établi un parallèle entre la présentation des résultats du Pasec 2024 et les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (Joj), que le Sénégal accueille à partir du 31 octobre. Deux rendez-vous différents, mais portés, selon lui, par une même ambition : préparer une jeunesse « éduquée, formée et outillée » pour relever les défis de son époque. Il a rappelé que les enseignants et les élèves restent les premiers concernés par les résultats des évaluations, dont la finalité est de rendre l’école plus juste et plus efficace. Il a également insisté sur la nécessité de rapprocher les outils d’évaluation des réalités quotidiennes des établissements scolaires. Les résultats doivent, a-t-il rappelé, éclairer les choix des pouvoirs publics et bénéficier directement aux élèves. Le gouvernement sénégalais examinera par ailleurs, avec le secrétaire général de la Confemen, les possibilités d’accompagner l’institution dans la recherche d’un cadre de travail adapté à l’élargissement de ses missions et de ses équipes. Pour le représentant du chef de l’État, les travaux de Dakar devront déboucher sur des recommandations réalistes et applicables, afin que les résultats du Pasec se traduisent par des améliorations concrètes dans les salles de classe. Par Daouda DIOUF

items.title: Ex-envoy faults Ortom’s use of words, remarks on Alia, governance in Benue
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Former Speaker of the Benue State House of Assembly and Nigeria’s former Ambassador to Namibia, Terhemen Tarzoor, has faulted former Governor Samuel Ortom over his reported remarks against Governor Hyacinth Alia and his administration urging political leaders to exercise restraint in their public engagements. Tarzoor, who spoke with newsmen in Makurdi, described some of Chief Ortom’s comments during a recent television programme as inappropriate, arguing that political differences should not undermine the dignity of the office of the governor or the people of the state. The former lawmaker, who is also the Benue State coordinator of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors for President Bola Tinubu 2027, said Ortom whom he described as an elder brother he respects, should be more measured in his public statements about the incumbent governor. “My take is that the former governor should not call the number one citizen 419. He has no right to call him that,” Tarzoor said, reacting to Ortom’s alleged description of Alia as a “419” and a “fake Reverend Father.” He also faulted Ortom’s reported comparison of the administration of Benue State to a Catholic parish, where priests allegedly collect offerings and spend the money without being questioned, Tarzoor, a Knight of St. John International, defended the Church’s financial management system, insisting that it operates established structures for accountability. “As a Knight of St. John International, I want to disabuse his mind and the minds of people who listened to that programme that there is a high level of accountability in the Catholic Church,” he said. “There is no Catholic priest that can just earn money and spend at ease in the Catholic Church,” he said, adding that political leaders should avoid statements that could be interpreted as questioning the integrity of religious institutions without sufficient knowledge of their operations. Tarzoor also criticised what he described as an unfair comparison between Ortom’s eight-year administration and Alia’s government, which has been in office for just over three years. He argued that any meaningful assessment of their performances must take into account the period each administration has spent in office and the targets set for them. “In comparative statistics, you talk about time-frame equality and goal equality before you can compare and contrast,” he said. The former Speaker further expressed concern over Ortom’s reported reference to some Benue people as “shenanigans,” describing the expression as inappropriate. “I see that as repugnant. If he has issues, he should apply the right language, apply decorum in the manner to address matters. That is the only legacy we can leave for our children, those yet unborn,” he said. On the issue of former governors’ entitlements, Tarzoor said he was unaware of any law providing for the benefits Ortom reportedly claimed were denied him, including a house in Abuja or elsewhere in the country and sponsorship of medical check-ups. “When I was Speaker, we never had such a law anywhere,” he said, while acknowledging that he could not speak definitively on whether such legislation had been enacted after he left office. “Any legitimate concerns over entitlements could be addressed through appropriate channels rather than public exchanges,” he said. The former Ambassador maintained that the Alia administration was open to scrutiny, urging the media and members of the public to seek accurate information on government revenue and expenditure through established procedures, including the Freedom of Information framework. “Governor Hyacinth Alia is open to all criticisms. The law is clear on freedom of information. You test it; the records will be there for you to see,” he said, urging political leaders to promote constructive engagement and accountability. The post Ex-envoy faults Ortom’s use of words, remarks on Alia, governance in Benue appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Guinée: taux de croissance et d’inflation, déficit budgétaire, recettes et dépenses, le tableau de bord de l’économie présenté aux députés
items.description: Devant l’Assemblée nationale, ce samedi 24 octobre 2026, la ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget, Mariama Ciré Sylla, a présenté le projet de loi de finances rectificative (LFR) 2026. Au cœur de cette révision budgétaire, la protection du pouvoir d’achat, la mobilisation des recettes publiques, la maîtrise du déficit et la réorientation des investissements liés au programme Simandou 2040. Des chiffres qui traduisent les arbitrages du gouvernement face aux tensions économiques internationales et aux besoins sociaux du pays. C’est avec émotion et un sens affirmé du devoir que Mariama Ciré Sylla s’est exprimée pour la première fois devant les députés de la dixième législature. A la tribune de l’Assemblée nationale, la ministre a défendu un budget rectificatif qu’elle présente comme un instrument d’adaptation aux nouvelles réalités économiques, financières et sociales, mais aussi comme un levier pour rapprocher davantage l’État des citoyens. Au-delà des ajustements comptables, le gouvernement entend préserver les priorités sociales tout en révisant certaines dépenses et prévisions initiales. Au 15 octobre 2026, les recettes mobilisées atteignaient 44 225 milliards de francs guinéens, soit 85 % des prévisions de recettes de la loi de finances initiale. A la même date, les engagements de dépenses s’élevaient à 29 982 milliards de francs guinéens, selon les chiffres communiqués par la ministre. Ces données constituent le point de départ d’une révision budgétaire destinée à tenir compte de l’évolution de la conjoncture et des besoins de financement de l’État. L’un des principaux enjeux de cette LFR concerne le maintien du prix des produits pétroliers à 12 000 francs guinéens le litre. Face à la volatilité des cours internationaux de l’énergie, aux tensions géopolitiques et aux perturbations des chaînes d’approvisionnement, la Guinée a choisi de limiter les répercussions de ces chocs sur les ménages et les activités économiques. Pour soutenir cette politique, le gouvernement prévoit une enveloppe de 5 489 milliards de francs guinéens consacrée au mécanisme de subvention des produits pétroliers. Cette somme représente, selon la ministre, environ 10 % des recettes fiscales prévues dans le projet de budget rectificatif. A cela s’ajoute la prise en compte de pertes de recettes liées aux mesures consenties sur les produits pétroliers, évaluées à environ 4 576,7 milliards de francs guinéens. L’effort financier est considérable. Il traduit la volonté affichée de protéger le pouvoir d’achat, mais soulève également la question de la soutenabilité du dispositif et de ses conséquences sur les marges budgétaires disponibles pour les autres secteurs prioritaires. La ministre a ainsi insisté sur la nécessité de renforcer la transparence, le suivi et la traçabilité de ce mécanisme afin de préserver les capacités de financement de la santé, de l’éducation et des investissements productifs. Sur le plan macroéconomique, les prévisions sont également réajustées. La croissance économique, estimée à 7,1 % en 2025, est désormais projetée à 6,6 % en 2026, selon les données présentées dans le discours. Le taux d’inflation moyen est, pour sa part, relevé à 5,2 %, contre 3,5 % initialement prévu. Ces révisions reflètent notamment les incertitudes internationales et leurs effets sur les prix, les importations et les équilibres économiques. La ministre a également mis en avant les résultats attribués à la digitalisation des administrations fiscales et douanières. Selon les chiffres qu’elle a présentés, les recettes concernées ont doublé entre 2023 et 2024, puis progressé de 50 % entre 2024 et 2025. Le gouvernement entend poursuivre cette dynamique en limitant les pertes de recettes, en améliorant le recouvrement et en veillant à ce que les ressources collectées profitent davantage aux populations. Du côté des dépenses, le projet de LFR prévoit une augmentation globale de 5,8 %, principalement portée par les dépenses courantes et les mesures de soutien aux ménages. En revanche, les dépenses d’investissement sont révisées à la baisse de 2 729 milliards de francs guinéens. Cette réduction est notamment liée à la revue des projets du programme Simandou 2040, avec l’objectif affiché de privilégier les projets suffisamment préparés et de reporter ceux qui nécessitent encore des études complémentaires. Le déficit budgétaire est ainsi projeté à 2,01 % du PIB, contre 2,07 % initialement prévus. Le gouvernement affirme que ce déficit doit être couvert par des ressources de financement identifiées, afin de préserver l’équilibre du budget rectificatif. Pour Mariama Ciré Sylla, ces mesures doivent permettre de traduire les ressources publiques en services concrets : des centres de santé fonctionnels, des écoles mieux accompagnées, des administrations plus accessibles et davantage de possibilités économiques pour les jeunes. L’enjeu consiste désormais à mesurer l’efficacité de ces allocations à travers les résultats obtenus sur le terrain.

items.title: North Korea's Kim returns home after visit to Chinese border city
items.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un returned home on Saturday after a day-long trip to the Chinese border city of Dandong, Beijing’s state media reported , though the purpose of the unannounced visit was not immediately clear. Kim is thought to have crossed into China via a major border bridge that officially opened last week — 12 years after its completion — deepening economic ties between China and diplomatically isolated North Korea. Neither North Korea nor China disclosed Kim’s visit in advance. South Korean lawmaker Youn Kun-young said Kim was “understood” to have met Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Saturday. A readout from China’s Xinhua news agency did not mention talks between Kim and Chinese President Xi Jinping or Li. Instead, it said Wang Huning, Beijing’s top political adviser, accompanied Kim in Dandong and “saw him off” at the bridge at the end of the trip. The aims and outcomes of Kim’s visit were murky, but China is North Korea’s largest trading partner and a vital source of diplomatic, economic and political support for Pyongyang. Xinhua quoted Wang as saying the visit was significant for “consolidating public goodwill towards the friendship (and) deepening political mutual trust and jointly pursuing cooperation and development”. Wang conveyed Xi’s “cordial greetings and best wishes” to the North Korean leader. The trip fell near the date both countries use to mark the entry of Chinese troops into the Korean War. Kim attended a memorial ceremony to fallen soldiers and visited an automobile factory, Xinhua said. China’s top diplomat, Wang Yi, also participated in the events, it added. Youn, the South Korean lawmaker, said he had been briefed on Friday that a visit was likely. In Dandong late on Saturday, the bridge stood empty and the surrounding neighbourhood was quiet. Resident Zhao told AFP it was “quite good” that Kim visited, saying he feels that a closer relationship between the two countries could ultimately benefit his city. “When the two countries engage with each other, it will naturally benefit border cities in China economically,” the 50-year-old driver said. “We have high hopes for that. May our friendship last forever.” Bridging a divide The New Yalu River Bridge was completed in 2014, but its opening was delayed due to a lack of connecting roads and customs facilities on the North Korean side, according to South Korean news reports. Its opening came just over a month after North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge. Kim may have sought to “press China to move more quickly” on commitments agreed during Xi’s visit to North Korea this year, Yang Moo-jin, former president of the South’s University of North Korean Studies, told AFP . “He may also have sought Beijing’s active support and cooperation ahead of a possible summit with [US President Donald] Trump in Shenzhen.” Hours before South Korea’s Yonhap news agency first reported Saturday’s visit, North Korean state media said Kim had urged his military at a major meeting in Pyongyang to train to become the strongest in the world. Kim’s call for what he dubbed a “Korean-style military revolution” came soon after Seoul’s military proposed talks to clarify the shared border with the North, following an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone. Seoul’s military proposed the talks on Friday after it blamed the blast, which injured South Korean soldiers and severely strained bilateral relations, on North Korean landmines. Pyongyang strongly rejects the claim. North Korea has not responded to the proposal and previously rejected the South’s demand for an apology over the explosion. The countries remain technically at war as their 1950-53 conflict ended in an armistice, not a peace treaty. Implicit acceptance Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime routinely declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible . South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung — who has repeatedly offered Pyongyang talks without preconditions — suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of North Korea’s nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief. Critics say such an approach risks tacitly accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to win sanctions relief without giving up its arsenal. Analysts say China has also appeared to move towards implicit acceptance. Kim hosted Xi in Pyongyang in June, soon after Xi held back-to-back summits in Beijing with Trump and Russia’s Vladimir Putin. Neither Pyongyang nor Beijing mentioned North Korean denuclearisation in their official statements after the June meeting — an omission experts saw as a sign of China’s tacit consent.

items.title: Tottenham seal rare win at Chelsea as Palmer sees red
items.description: Tottenham clinched a Premier League win at Chelsea for just the second time in 36 years as a woeful own goal from Blues keeper Mike Penders was followed by Cole Palmer’s red card in Saturday’s 2-0 victory. Roberto De Zerbi’s side clinched their second successive league win thanks to Penders’s howler in the second half at a rain-lashed Stamford Bridge. Chelsea forward Palmer was sent off for a second booking moments later before Mathys Tel produced a superb solo effort to condemn the Blues to their first home defeat against Tottenham since 2018. Since 1990, Tottenham had won just once in 41 previous away matches against London rivals Chelsea in all competitions. Ending that miserable run gave Tottenham only their second win in their last 16 league games against Chelsea, both home and away, and their first since 2023. After a dismal start to the season, Tottenham have climbed to 12th place after building on Monday’s win against Coventry, which ended their wait for a first league win this season. It was a bitter blow for fourth-placed Chelsea, who had beaten Bournemouth and Everton in their previous two league games. They were booed off at full-time and remain very much a work in progress under Xabi Alonso in the Spaniard’s first season in charge. With Joao Pedro sidelined by a late injury, Morgan Rogers was Chelsea’s central striker, but their revamped attack was short of bite. Teed up by Rogers after Pedro Neto stole possession from Mateus Fernandes, Palmer went close to an early opener with a curler that Antonin Kinsky tipped over at full stretch. Tottenham responded with a spell of probing pressure as Omar Marmoush met Andy Robertson’s cross with a shot that was repelled by Penders. Alonso’s men pieced together the best move of the half with a flurry of one-touch passes to reach Jordan Henderson on the edge of the area, but the midfielder’s low drive was palmed away by Kinsky. – Spurs spring a surprise – Neto tested Kinsky with a fierce blast but the Tottenham keeper was up to the task with a save at his near post. Tottenham suffered a blow when often-injured midfielder James Maddison limped off in a premature end to only his second start since May 2025. Maddison had already missed training sessions since his long-awaited start against Coventry and his latest fitness setback suggested it was a failed gamble to start him at the Bridge. In keeping with the sloppy fare, Neto fired straight at Kinsky from a dangerous position after Palmer pounced on Sandro Tonali’s wayward pass. When Palmer’s run was halted by Fernandes’s handball, the Chelsea star escaped with a yellow card after barging into his rival with such aggression that the Tottenham midfielder was sent crashing to the sodden turf. Tottenham exacted swift revenge in the 77th minute. Fernandes’s in-swinging corner should have been caught by Penders, but he opted for a punch that was completely mistimed as he diverted the ball into his net for a comical own goal. It was a horrible moment for the 21-year-old Penders, who was making his first league start in the absence of Emiliano Martinez following jaw surgery. Rubbing salt into Chelsea’s wounds, Palmer was dismissed three minutes later for an ugly stamp on Conor Gallagher. Tel wrapped up Tottenham’s memorable triumph in fitting style in the 87th minute, skipping away from Chelsea’s flat-footed defence to drill a fine finish into the bottom corner from the edge of the area. The post Tottenham seal rare win at Chelsea as Palmer sees red appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Makinde faults Tinubu over foreign reserves claim, says Nigerians still hungry
items.description: .As APM launches reset movement in Lagos By Olasunkanmi Akoni Oyo State Governor and Presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has accused President Bola Tinubu of using reported growth in foreign reserves to create impression of economic recovery which is untrue. Makinde accused Tinubu’s administration, of using rising foreign reserve figures as a “political gimmick” to obscure widespread hunger and economic distress across the nation. ​Speaking via online video message on Saturday at the launch of the Makinde and Daura for Better Nigeria (MAD) Resetter Movement in Lagos, Makinde maintained that boasting about macroeconomic growth means nothing to millions of citizens struggling daily to afford basic necessities. “I am with you 101 per cent towards the reset agenda for Nigeria. We need to reset our economy, our security architecture, our educational system and the socio-political environment,” he said. Makinde likened the situation to a household where the head boasts of savings while family members go hungry. “We have heard stories that Nigeria’s foreign reserves are going up. I liken it to a household where the head is telling the people that we have a lot of money in our savings accounts, but everyone in that household is hungry,” he said. Makinde said economic progress should be measured by citizens’ prosperity and ability to pursue opportunities, and called for return to federalism and multiparty democracy. “Nigeria was negotiated on the basis of a federalism arrangement. Nigeria was negotiated on the basis of multiparty democracy,” he said. ​Comparing the government’s stance to a flawed household dynamic, Makinde stated; “We have heard stories that Nigeria’s foreign reserves are going up. I liken it to a household where the head is telling the people that we have a lot of money in our savings accounts, but everyone in that household is hungry.” ​APM Presidential candidate, stressed that true economic progress must be judged by tangible improvements in living standards, job opportunities for young people, and financial independence, rather than official statistics. ​Calling for a comprehensive national reset, Makinde urged Nigerians to look beyond propaganda and demand a return to genuine federalism and multiparty democracy. He called on citizens across all geopolitical zones to join the movement to reshape the country’s economic, educational, security, and socio-political frameworks ahead of the 2027 general elections. ​Also, Director-General of the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, Hassan Felix, questioned the government’s claims of economic recovery. Citing rising unemployment, worsening insecurity, and the departure of foreign companies from Nigeria, Felix stated that the “time of deceit is over” and demanded an immediate change in direction. ​Similarly, Director of Volunteers and Support Groups for the campaign, Dr. Emmanuel Dennis, stressed that the movement intends to break away from traditional political rallies focused merely on entertainment. ​”We want to make our campaign issue-based,” Dennis said, pointing to soaring petrol prices, stagnant salaries, and erosion of electoral integrity through judicial outcomes rather than voter choice,” Dennis stated. He therefore, urged supporters to back the movement in resetting governance both in Lagos State and at the federal level. ​APM pledges inclusive governance in Lagos ​The launch also featured the endorsement of APM’s Lagos State governorship candidate, Adelaja Adeoye, along with the party’s senatorial and legislative flagbearers, by local government party chairmen represented by Isiaka Sodeinde. ​Pledging an inclusive, gender-sensitive administration free from the influence of political godfathers, Adeoye urged voters to resist vote-buying ahead of the polls. ​”Your PVC is the instrument in your hands; that is your power,” Adeoye told supporters. “If truly you are tired of bad governance, don’t collect money from them. Don’t let them bribe you because what they give you won’t last you a day,” Adeoye stated. The post Makinde faults Tinubu over foreign reserves claim, says Nigerians still hungry appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PLFR 2026 : Les arbitrages expliqués par le gouvernement ce dimanche
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô, tiendra une conférence de presse ce dimanche 25 octobre 2026, à 16 heures, au Building administratif Président Mamadou Dia, après le rejet du projet de loi de finances rectificative (PLFR) 2026 par la Commission des Finances et du Contrôle budgétaire de l’Assemblée nationale. L’examen du texte a débuté le mardi 20 octobre. Les députés ont notamment interrogé le Gouvernement sur «les prévisions de recettes, les arbitrages budgétaires, la programmation des investissements publics ainsi que les subventions à la consommation d’énergie», indique un communiqué de la Primature. Les travaux, suspendus pour permettre à l’Exécutif de répondre aux préoccupations des parlementaires, ont repris le vendredi 23 octobre avec la présentation d’un mémorandum de réponses. Malgré ces clarifications, la Commission a rejeté le projet de loi, souligne la même source. Cette conférence de presse sera l’occasion pour le Gouvernement de présenter «les analyses économiques et financières qui sous-tendent le PLFR 2026 » et d’expliquer les orientations budgétaires retenues. Selon la Primature, la mise en œuvre du projet vise à «améliorer la qualité de vie des Sénégalais». Le gouvernement du Sénégal réaffirme « son attachement au dialogue institutionnel, à la transparence dans la gestion des finances publiques et à l’information des citoyens », note le communiqué.

items.title: Nayi Alhassan retains NDC Tema North chairmanship as Salman Faris wins secretary
items.description: Nayi Alhassan, popularly known as Ngbagu, has retained his position as National Democratic Congress (NDC) chairman for the Tamale North Constituency after securing 518 votes in the party’s constituency executive elections. He defeated Salifu Mohammed, who polled 352 votes, and Abdul Halim Wayo Issahaku, who obtained 147 votes. In the race for constituency secretary, Salman Faris Inusah emerged victorious with 598 votes, beating Baba Alhassan, popularly known as Mr Law, who secured 423 votes. Mutala Hussein won the vice-chairmanship position with 476 votes, defeating Mohammed Nurideen Iddrisu, popularly known as Zaachi, who obtained 428 votes. Abdulai Abdul Rahaman received 107 votes. Iddrisu Mohammed Nurideen won the deputy secretary position with 519 votes, narrowly beating Salman Iddrisu, who polled 502 votes. For the treasurer position, Mateen Mohammed secured 639 votes, while Alhassan Adam, popularly known as Sahanaa, won the deputy treasurer position with 597 votes. Baba Tahiru was elected communications officer after polling 774 votes to defeat Yussif Tikuma, who obtained 246 votes. Abdullah Abdul Rafiu, popularly known as Ras King, won the deputy communications officer position with 659 votes. Results for other positions In the organiser race, Mohammed A. Issahak emerged winner with 424 votes. He was followed by Issahaku Abdulai, popularly known as Captain America, with 279 votes, and Issahaku Alidu Bako, known as CR7, with 212 votes. Alhassan Abubakar, popularly known as Mr Abu, polled 88 votes, while Issah Zakaria Sasqo received nine votes. Nashiru Iddrisu, popularly known as Prince Nash, won the deputy organiser position with 500 votes. Abdul Wadud Mohammed received 289 votes, Alhassan Abdul Latif Napari secured 123 votes, and Abdul Mumin Seidu, known as Hon Kporo, polled 106 votes. Alidu Mohammed won the youth organiser position with 99 votes, ahead of Issahaku Amin, who received 16 votes. Husaifa Alhassan won deputy youth organiser with 82 votes, defeating Abdallah Jalil Yussif, who polled 32 votes. Ayishatu Abdulai Yahaya emerged women’s organiser with 63 votes, beating Ruhiya Adam, who secured 48 votes. In the deputy women’s organiser contest, Suweiba Iddrisu Alhassan won with 37 votes. Diana Alhassan obtained 35 votes, Memuna Sumani received 30 votes, and Sadia Abubakar polled eight votes. Alhassan Mohammed Sadat secured 381 votes in the treasurer race, finishing behind winner Mateen Mohammed, who obtained 639 votes. In the deputy treasurer contest, Zakaria Abass, popularly known as Oly, received 423 votes, losing to Alhassan Adam, who secured 597 votes. For deputy communications officer, Abdulai Ibrahim Danaa polled 187 votes, while Tahiru Lansah received 174 votes, both behind winner Abdullah Abdul Rafiu, who secured 659 votes. In the Zongo Caucus election, Adizatu Suleman won with 555 votes, defeating Sulemana Ahmed, who polled 350 votes, and Amadu Mohammed, who obtained 166 votes. The elections form part of the NDC’s nationwide constituency-level reorganisation exercise aimed at electing executives to coordinate party activities and strengthen grassroots structures ahead of the 2028 general elections

items.title: Octobre Rose à Mamou : la LONAGUI organise le dépistage gratuit des cancers féminins
items.description: Dans le cadre d’Octobre Rose, la Loterie nationale de Guinée (LONAGUI) accompagne le Réseau national des femmes rurales de Guinée (RENAFERGUI) dans une campagne de dépistage gratuit des cancers du sein et du col de l’utérus. Lancée ce samedi 24 octobre 2026 à Mamou, cette initiative vise à renforcer la sensibilisation et à faciliter l’accès des femmes aux services de dépistage, notamment en milieu rural. Chaque année, le mois d’octobre est consacré à la sensibilisation et à la mobilisation contre les cancers du sein et du col de l’utérus. À Mamou, cette campagne bénéficie de l’appui financier et institutionnel de la LONAGUI, qui entend contribuer à la prévention de ces maladies et promouvoir une prise en charge précoce des patientes. Cet engagement s’inscrit dans la volonté de l’entreprise publique de soutenir les initiatives sociales et sanitaires, particulièrement en faveur des populations vulnérables, pour lesquelles l’accès aux services de santé spécialisés demeure parfois difficile. Prenant la parole au nom de la LONAGUI, Jacqueline Coker, conseillère du directeur général et directrice des ressources humaines (DRH), a réaffirmé l’engagement de son institution en faveur de la santé des populations. « Face à cet enjeu de santé publique, la Loterie nationale de Guinée (LONAGUI) ne pouvait rester en marge. En tant qu’entreprise profondément citoyenne, notre institution a fait le choix de placer le bien-être des populations au cœur de ses actions », a-t-elle déclaré. Elle a précisé que cet accompagnement s’inscrit dans la politique de responsabilité sociétale des entreprises (RSE) de la LONAGUI, qui vise notamment à soutenir des actions concrètes au bénéfice des communautés, y compris celles vivant à l’intérieur du pays. Selon Jacqueline Coker, le soutien apporté au RENAFERGUI traduit la volonté de contribuer à rendre le dépistage gratuit plus accessible aux femmes les plus vulnérables, en particulier celles résidant en milieu rural. S’adressant aux femmes, elle les a exhortées à ne pas céder à la peur et à se faire dépister sans attendre l’apparition de symptômes. « Le cancer n’est pas une fatalité. Dépisté tôt, le cancer se guérit. N’ayez pas peur et ne laissez pas la rumeur ou la crainte vous éloigner des centres de santé », a-t-elle lancé. De son côté, Mme Fatoumata, représentante du RENAFERGUI, a souligné que la lutte contre ces cancers ne saurait se limiter au dépistage. Elle a insisté sur la nécessité d’assurer un suivi effectif aux femmes dont les résultats nécessitent des examens complémentaires ou un traitement. Elle a notamment évoqué les difficultés financières auxquelles sont confrontées certaines patientes, qui peuvent compromettre la poursuite de leur parcours de soins. « L’accompagnement des malades, c’est la partie la plus lourde et la plus coûteuse de notre campagne. Mais c’est aussi celle qui sauve des vies. Dépister sans accompagner, c’est montrer la porte à une femme sans l’aider à la franchir », a-t-elle expliqué. Dans cette perspective, la représentante du RENAFERGUI a sollicité un renforcement de l’appui de la LONAGUI afin de permettre aux femmes concernées de bénéficier d’un accompagnement allant du dépistage jusqu’au traitement. « Le chemin est encore loin et les besoins sont grands. Mais avec vous, nous pouvons réussir », a-t-elle conclu. Représentant le gouverneur de la région de Mamou, Mamadou Saliou Diallo, chef de cabinet au gouvernorat, a salué l’engagement de la LONAGUI en faveur de la santé des femmes et de l’amélioration des conditions de vie des communautés. Il a estimé que cette initiative contribue à promouvoir le progrès social et un meilleur accès aux soins, tout en réaffirmant la disponibilité des autorités régionales à accompagner la campagne. « Nous saluons le soutien de la LONAGUI, qui s’engage constamment pour l’amélioration des conditions de vie de nos communautés et pour la cause des femmes », a-t-il déclaré. À Mamou, cette campagne d’Octobre Rose met en lumière l’importance du dépistage précoce, de la sensibilisation et du suivi médical des patientes. Au-delà de la mobilisation ponctuelle du mois d’octobre, le défi reste de garantir un accès durable aux soins et de lever les obstacles financiers et sociaux qui empêchent encore certaines femmes de bénéficier d’une prise en charge adaptée.

items.title: ADC mocks APC over ‘rented crowds, empty seats’ at Kaduna rally
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has mocked the All Progressives Congress, APC, over what it described as a disappointing Northwest zonal flag-off rally in Kaduna, alleging that rented crowds and empty seats exposed the ruling party’s declining public acceptance. The council said the rally, which was intended to showcase the APC’s political strength across the Northwest, fell short of expectations despite alleged mobilisation of attendees from the seven states in the zone and beyond. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC alleged that attendees were reportedly paid between ₦50,000 and ₦100,000 each, yet the Kaduna Township Stadium, which it put at a capacity of 5,000, remained sparsely occupied. “For a rally billed as the Northwest zonal flag-off, what we witnessed was a shameful spectacle. Despite the alleged mobilisation of crowds from across the zone and beyond, the stadium remained scantily filled, with empty seats everywhere,” Ologbondiyan said. He also faulted the reception given to speeches by APC leaders, describing it as unenthusiastic and at odds with the ruling party’s attempt to project political strength in the region. The ADC-PCC further questioned President Bola Tinubu’s performance claims, criticising his reported commissioning of road projects at the rally. Ologbondiyan alleged that some attendees expressed dissatisfaction with the APC after leaving the stadium, chanting “Ba mu yi,” a Hausa expression he interpreted as a rejection of the ruling party and its policies. “You can rent a crowd, but you cannot rent acceptance. Even if people attend a rally, that does not mean they have surrendered their convictions. The real test of public support is what Nigerians will decide at the ballot box,” he said. The council accused the APC of recycling promises made during the 2015, 2019 and 2023 election cycles without adequately accounting for its years in power. It also accused Tinubu of shifting responsibility for Nigerians’ economic hardship to opposition leaders instead of addressing the consequences of his administration’s policies, particularly fuel subsidy removal, which it said had intensified the pressure on households struggling with rising living costs. The ADC-PCC urged the ruling party to abandon what it called wasteful political jamborees, apologise to Nigerians over the prevailing economic difficulties and prepare for an orderly transfer of power in 2027. The council maintained that the ADC offered a credible alternative to the APC, expressing confidence that voters would use the next general election to reject the ruling party. “The message from Kaduna is loud and clear: Nigerians are saying ‘Ba mu yi’ to the APC and Tinubu. Come 2027, they will speak even louder with their votes,” Ologbondiyan declared. The post ADC mocks APC over ‘rented crowds, empty seats’ at Kaduna rally appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Liga : Yassir Zabiri offre la victoire au Racing de Santander face à l’Espanyol
items.description: L’attaquant marocain Yassir Zabiri a offert une précieuse victoire au Racing de Santander face à l’Espanyol Barcelone (2-1), en inscrivant le but décisif à cinq minutes de la fin de la rencontre, permettant à son équipe de renouer avec le succès et de s’éloigner de la zone de relégation. Alors que les deux formations étaient à égalité (1-1), l’international marocain a surgi dans la surface de réparation à la suite d’un corner pour pousser le ballon au fond des filets et sceller la remontée des Cantabres. Grâce à cette réalisation, Zabiri porte à huit son nombre de buts inscrits cette saison, confirmant son rôle déterminant dans le dispositif offensif du Racing de Santander. Après une première période sans but, l’Espanyol avait ouvert le score par l’intermédiaire d’Edu Expósito, à la suite d’une contre-attaque menée par Javi Hernández. Le Racing a rapidement réagi en égalisant cinq minutes plus tard grâce à une puissante frappe croisée de Belocian, avant que Zabiri ne donne définitivement l’avantage aux siens dans les dernières minutes. Ce succès permet au Racing de Santander de mettre fin à une série de résultats décevants et de se repositionner au milieu du classement, tandis que cette nouvelle défaite fragilise davantage l’avenir de l’entraîneur de l’Espanyol, Manolo González. Le club cantabre accueillera dimanche prochain le Real Madrid au stade El Sardinero, pour la première fois depuis quatorze ans. items.title: Cien detenidos por los disturbios en el centro de Barcelona
items.description: Centenares de jóvenes se han concentrado este sábado en Barcelona y han destrozado el mobiliario urbano, han provocado daños en bicicletas y motos y saqueado 14 comercios. Los Mossos d’Esquadra y la Guàrdia Urbana han organizado un gran despliegue con más de 220 agentes para frenar los actos vandálicos, haciendo conatos de cargas contra los encapuchados que se ha saldado de momento con un centenar de detenidos, un 25% de ellos menores. Muchos comercios y restaurantes han cerrado para evitar daños y saqueos en la plaza Catalunya, la Rambla, la avenida del Portal de l’Àngel y las calles adyacentes. Los jóvenes han acudido al centro convocados a través de las redes en una manifestación no comunicada. El Ayuntamiento ha blindado la plaza y las calles del entorn, desde la plaza de Urquinaona a la de la Universitat. El president Salvador Illa ha condenado los actos violentos : “La violencia no tiene cabida en Cataluña. Nunca. Protestar es un derecho democrático. Agreder, intimidar y causar destrozos no lo es”. items.title: Ellen White Foundation brings free breast cancer screening to Bono East police women
items.description: In a heartwarming display of commitment to women’s health, the Ellen White Sustainable Foundation, in partnership with the Awat Foundation and the Police Ladies Association, has provided free breast cancer screening to nearly 100 female police officers across the Bono East Region. The screening exercise, held at the Techiman Divisional Police Command, formed part of efforts to promote early detection and awareness of breast cancer among women in uniform. The programme was held under the theme: “Investing in Women’s Health, Investing in Stronger Communities.” Mrs. Ellen White Opoku, founder of the Ellen White Sustainable Foundation and a 2023 Joy Impact Makers Award recipient, said the initiative was born out of the need to reach officers who cannot easily access health facilities due to their busy schedules. “This exercise is to help bring the screening to the doorstep of the police, who are unable to attend to health facilities for the same due to their busy work schedules,” she noted. Police Ladies Association Weighs In ASP Beatrice Okrah, Crime Officer for the Jema District Police Command and a regional executive member of the Police Ladies Association, commended the organizers and encouraged women to prioritize their health. She said the time had come for women to own up and get themselves screened to know their statuses and be treated when diagnosed with the condition. “The time has come for women to own up and get themselves screened to know their statuses and be treated when diagnosed with the condition,” she stated. ASP Okrah added that the awareness talk had been helpful in creating awareness about what the condition is, equipping participants with knowledge to share with colleagues and family members. “The talk has been helpful in creating awareness about what the condition is,” she noted. Service to Support Officers Diagnosed In a reassuring message to personnel, ASP Okrah disclosed that officers found to have the cancer will be taken care of by the Police Service. She explained that the welfare of officers remains a priority, and those diagnosed through the screening will receive the necessary support and care from the Service. A Community Investment The event reflects a growing push to make healthcare accessible to women in security services, who often sacrifice personal wellness for public duty. By investing in the health of these officers, organizers say the ripple effect will be felt across entire communities. The Ellen White Sustainable Foundation has indicated its commitment to sustaining such initiatives, with plans to reach more districts in the Bono East Region and beyond.

items.title: Ghana’s U-15 Boys thrash Uzbekistan 4-1 as Abdul Aziz Issah and Jerry Owusu hit brace each
items.description: The National U-15 Boys team made a flying start to the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Uzbekistan in their opening Group W match on Saturday. Abdul Aziz Issah and Jerry Owusu were the heroes for Ghana, scoring a brace each to secure all three points in Azerbaijan. Ghana dominated proceedings from the blast of the whistle, showing flair, composure and attacking intent against their Asian opponents. Aziz Issah opened the scoring before doubling Ghana’s advantage, while Jerry Owusu added two more goals to put the game beyond the reach of Uzbekistan, who managed a consolation strike late in the game. The win gives Ghana a strong start in Group W, which also includes Myanmar, Guam, Bahamas and Kazakhstan. Ghana will next face Myanmar and Guam on Sunday, before wrapping up the group phase against Bahamas and Kazakhstan on Monday. The FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival, part of FIFA’s Talent Development Scheme, is aimed at giving every talent a chance to showcase their skills on the world stage.

items.title: GH¢49.72m S.A. evacuation: Asafo-Adjei says government’s figures do not add up
items.description: The Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Nana Asafo-Adjei Ayeh, has raised concerns over the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa, insisting that the figures presented by the government do not add up. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, the opposition lawmaker questioned the credibility of the expenditure, arguing that the inability to satisfactorily establish the number of beneficiaries raises serious concerns about the entire evacuation exercise. “I am at this point confident in everything in me that the figures don’t add up. If you cannot even establish the 1,964, then there is a problem with everything you did,” he stated. Mr Asafo-Adjei maintained that the documents presented to justify the expenditure must be subjected to thorough scrutiny, stressing that the details should support the government’s public explanations. According to him, the Minority’s concerns are based on the contents of the available documentation rather than political disagreements or unrelated issues. “The content of the document is what matters. The devil is always in the details, and that is what we are looking at, and it doesn’t support your communication,” he said. The Deputy Ranking Member emphasised that his focus remains on establishing the facts surrounding the expenditure and ensuring that the government provides satisfactory explanations for the amount spent and the reported number of evacuees. He rejected suggestions that the Minority was diverting attention from the substantive issues, insisting that his interventions have consistently centred on accountability and transparency. “If you listen to the Minority, particularly me, I have never majored in any tangential. I am focused on this matter, and I want to get to the logical conclusion of this matter,” he stressed. His comments come amid scrutiny of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs over the reported GH¢49.72 million expenditure on the evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa.
