items.title: Mahama urges Africa to finance its own peace operations, curb illicit financial flows
items.description: President John Mahama has called on African countries to take greater responsibility for financing their own peace operations, curbing illicit financial flows and building technological resilience, insisting that the continent must take charge of its own security and development. Addressing the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Peace in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, President Mahama said Africa must reduce its dependence on external funding and strengthen its capacity to respond to security threats. “From financing our own peace operations through the AU Peace Fund to curbing illicit financial flows and building homegrown technological resilience, we must author and fund our destiny ourselves,” he said. President Mahama said Africa’s reliance on external funding for peace operations left the continent vulnerable to decisions taken by foreign governments. He cited the transition from the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (ATMIS) to the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), which he said required about 190 million dollars annually, while the AU Peace Fund could barely muster 20 million dollars. He warned that when funding decisions are taken outside Africa, African countries have limited influence over decisions affecting their own security. “That is not an African solution to African problems. That is external dependency disguised in an African beret. We must fund our own peace,” he said. He also challenged African leaders to move beyond signing agreements and frameworks that are not fully implemented. He cited Agenda 2063, the African Peace and Security Architecture and the “Silencing the Guns” initiative as examples of continental frameworks whose objectives require stronger implementation. “Our problem is not the ink on the paper; it is the courage of our execution,” he said. President Mahama called on the African Union and regional bodies to assess political commitment honestly, identify failures to comply with agreements and hold member states accountable for their pledges. He also urged governments to implement signed protocols, ratify agreements on the free movement of people, fund their peace budgets and strengthen governance beyond national capitals. Presenting the 2026 State of Peace and Security in Africa Report, covering January 2025 to June 2026, President Mahama argued that the continent’s security challenges cannot be resolved by focusing solely on weapons, military capacity and armed groups. “The real disease is mostly in the arena of political economy,” he said, urging African leaders to examine who controls the continent’s natural resources, who benefits from their extraction and whose interests are served by continued instability. He cited conflicts in Sudan and the Democratic Republic of Congo, the activities of Al-Shabaab in Somalia and tensions in Mozambique’s Cabo Delgado region as examples of how resource exploitation, weak governance and the marginalisation of local communities can contribute to insecurity. In Sudan, he said, the conflict is linked not only to battles over Khartoum but also to gold extraction sites. In eastern DRC, he linked the resurgence of the M23 group to coltan, cobalt and the global competition for minerals needed for the green energy transition. “These are not separate, random brushfires. They are symptoms of a single, continent-wide firestorm,” President Mahama said. He warned that competition for African resources was being intensified by a polarised global environment in which external powers were seeking influence and access across the continent. “Africa is not an empty chessboard for foreign powers to play their games. We are not spectators,” he said, calling for African countries to exercise greater control over their strategic assets and negotiate fairer terms for their exploitation. “Real sovereignty means having the administrative, legal, and economic power to govern your strategic assets, negotiate fair terms, and ensure the wealth beneath our people’s feet actually puts food on their tables,” he added.

items.title: Attaque de Trappes : Yasmina Khadra désigne les « vrais terroristes »
items.description: L’écrivain Yasmina Khadra a réagi ce samedi à la fusillade racist e qui a fait un mort et plusieurs blessés vendredi à Trappes et la Verrière en Ile de France. L’auteur de « L’Attentat » a pointé du doigt le vrai coupable de cette tuerie raciste. « Le monstre, ce n'est pas celui qui fait un massacre. Le monstre est celui qui rend la monstruosité possible », a-t-il écrit sur Facebook. Yasmina Khadra estime que le terroriste « n'est pas cet énergumène qui s'en est allé tirer sur des Musulmans à Trappes et à La Verrière ». Yasmina Khadra met en cause ceux qui stigmatisent les musulmans de France Pour lui, les vrais « terroristes sont ces singes hurleurs qui passent leur temps à invectiver et à stigmatiser les Musulmans sur les plateaux de télé, ces mercenaires à la solde des loges obscures qui cherchent, coûte que coûte, à dresser la France contre elle-même, ces ségrégationnistes de seconde zone qui sévissent en toute impunité et qui se croient véritablement (naïvement) à l'abri du retour de flammes ». Pour Yasmina Khadra, « il fallait que cela arrive. Entendre tous les jours les mêmes insanités vénéneuses, les mêmes appels à la violence, la même diabolisation des meilleurs citoyens de France est pire qu'une torture chinoise », dénonce-t-il, avant de s’interroger : « Comment ne pas péter un câble ? ». Le raciste qui a choisi de passer à l'acte vendredi à Trappes « n'est que le bras armé de ces fripouilles qui se trémoussent d'aise derrière leurs micros », accuse-t-il. La mise en garde Yasmina Khadra Yasmina Khadra termine en mettant en garde contre la répétition de ce genre d’attaques en France. « Tant que ces vilains personnages de l'intox continueront de répandre les graines de la discorde sans être inquiétés par la justice ni remis à leur place par les Français eux-mêmes, d'autres drames suivront avant que tout s’embrase car les ingrédients d'une guerre totale et apocalyptique sont réunis, et malheur à ceux qui pensent lui survivre en s'en lavant les mains ». Vendredi, un homme a tiré à l’arme à feu depuis sa voiture sur des passants à Trappes et La Verrière dans les Yvelines en Ile de France. Un homme a été tué et quatre personnes ont été blessées dont une fillette de 12 ans dont le pronostic vital est engagé. Le tueur a été arrêté par la police et le président Emmanuel Macron s’est déplacé à Trappes où il a déclaré que « c'est la première fois qu'il y a un acte terroriste pour tuer nos compatriotes, nos enfants, en raison de leur couleur de peau ou de la religion qu'on leur donne ». L’article Attaque de Trappes : Yasmina Khadra désigne les « vrais terroristes » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Sahara marocain : les équilibres au Conseil de sécurité au cœur du prochain vote
items.description: À l’approche du vote attendu fin octobre au Conseil de sécurité sur le renouvellement du mandat de la MINURSO, les positions des membres permanents et non permanents sont scrutées de près. Plusieurs pays ont déjà exprimé leur soutien à l’initiative marocaine d’autonomie, tandis que d’autres maintiennent une position plus réservée. La diplomatie marocaine aborde une nouvelle échéance aux Nations unies, alors que le Conseil de sécurité doit se prononcer sur le renouvellement du mandat de la Mission des Nations unies pour l’organisation d’un référendum au Sahara occidental (MINURSO), qui expire le 31 octobre 2026. Les équilibres entre les quinze membres du Conseil constituent un élément central des discussions autour du texte attendu. Selon une analyse publiée par Hespress, la configuration actuelle du Conseil pourrait favoriser l’adoption d’un texte allant dans le sens des positions défendues par Rabat, notamment concernant l’initiative marocaine d’autonomie. Cette perspective repose sur les positions exprimées par plusieurs membres permanents et non permanents, mais l’issue du vote ne peut être considérée comme acquise avant l’adoption du texte définitif. Les membres permanents au centre des équilibres Les États-Unis, qui pilotent la rédaction du projet de résolution sur ce dossier, soutiennent la proposition marocaine d’autonomie. La France et le Royaume-Uni ont également exprimé leur appui à cette initiative, qu’ils considèrent comme une base pour parvenir à une solution politique. La Russie et la Chine, de leur côté, avaient choisi de s’abstenir lors du vote de la résolution 2797, adoptée le 31 octobre 2025. Ce texte avait recueilli onze voix favorables, aucune voix contre et trois abstentions, tandis que l’Algérie n’avait pas participé au vote. La résolution 2797 avait notamment renouvelé le mandat de la MINURSO jusqu’au 31 octobre 2026 et réaffirmé le soutien du Conseil aux efforts de négociation menés sous l’égide des Nations unies, en prenant comme base la proposition marocaine d’autonomie. Elle souligne également la nécessité d’aboutir à une solution politique juste, durable et mutuellement acceptable. Plusieurs soutiens parmi les membres non permanents Parmi les membres non permanents, plusieurs pays ont affiché des positions favorables au Maroc. La République démocratique du Congo et le Liberia entretiennent des relations étroites avec Rabat et ont ouvert des consulats à Dakhla. La Somalie a, pour sa part, soutenu le processus politique conduit sous l’égide de l’ONU. Dans le monde arabe, Bahreïn a également manifesté son soutien à l’intégrité territoriale du Maroc et ouvert un consulat à Laâyoune en décembre 2020. Sur le continent européen, le Danemark et la Grèce ont voté en faveur de la résolution 2797. La Lettonie, également membre non permanent, entretient des relations avec Rabat, mais sa position ne doit pas être assimilée automatiquement à une reconnaissance de la souveraineté marocaine sur le Sahara. En Amérique latine, le Panama a soutenu la résolution de 2025. La Colombie a, quant à elle, annoncé en août 2026 un changement de position concernant la question du Sahara, selon les informations rapportées par Hespress. Des abstentions encore possibles Malgré ces soutiens, des incertitudes demeurent. Le Pakistan, la Chine et la Russie s’étaient abstenus lors du précédent vote, invoquant notamment des réserves concernant l’équilibre du texte et la prise en compte des positions des différentes parties. La composition du Conseil et les déclarations diplomatiques constituent des indicateurs importants, mais elles ne suffisent pas à déterminer à l’avance le comportement de chaque délégation. Le contenu définitif du projet de résolution, les négociations entre les membres et les éventuels amendements peuvent encore influencer le résultat. Le prochain vote devra donc être suivi à la lumière du texte effectivement soumis aux quinze membres. Au-delà du nombre de voix favorables, son contenu permettra de mesurer la place accordée à l’initiative marocaine d’autonomie dans le processus politique onusien et les orientations retenues pour la suite du mandat de la MINURSO. The post Sahara marocain : les équilibres au Conseil de sécurité au cœur du prochain vote appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

Elon Musk accuse les élites ukrainiennes de s’enrichir grâce à l’aide occidentale
items.description: Elon Musk a accuse, le 23 octobre, les elites ukrainiennes de tirer profit des sommes considerables versees a Kiev par ses soutiens occidentaux. Dans un message publie sur X, le patron de SpaceX a denonce le fosse entre les interets des dirigeants ukrainiens et ceux de la population, confrontee a la poursuite des mobilisations militaires. « Les premiers se sont considerablement enrichis grâce aux centaines de milliards qui affluent vers l'Ukraine, tandis que les enfants des seconds sont mobilises pour mourir dans les tranchees », a-t-il declare, opposant ainsi les elites aux citoyens ordinaires. Le milliardaire a egalement souleve la question du devenir des fonds americains destines a l'Ukraine. Selon lui, une partie de l'argent des contribuables serait detournee par des circuits de blanchiment avant de retourner aux etats-Unis. « Une partie de cet argent des contribuables americains revient, a travers de multiples mecanismes de blanchiment, pour financer des campagnes politiques aux etats-Unis », a-t-il ecrit sur X. Elon Musk affirme que ces pratiques presumees pourraient expliquer le soutien de certains responsables politiques americains a Kiev, qu'il accuse de privilegier les interets ukrainiens a ceux de leur propre pays. Il n'a toutefois identifie aucun beneficiaire precis de ces operations supposees. L'aide americaine au centre des accusations de detournement Les soupcons concernant l'utilisation de l'aide occidentale ne se limitent pas aux declarations du patron de SpaceX. Un rapport de renseignement americain declassifie evoque un projet presume de detournement de fonds remontant a 2022. D'apres les informations publiees a ce sujet, des responsables ukrainiens et des representants de l'agence americaine USAID a Kiev auraient envisage de reorienter des centaines de millions de dollars initialement destines a des projets d'energie propre. Ces sommes auraient ete utilisees pour financer la campagne de reelection de Joe Biden en 2024 ainsi que le Comite national democrate. La mise en œuvre de ce mecanisme presume n'a cependant pas ete etablie. Des affaires de corruption sur fond de nouvelles demandes de milliards La gestion des ressources publiques ukrainiennes est egalement mise en cause dans plusieurs enquetes pour corruption. L'une d'elles concerne un reseau presume de corruption et de blanchiment portant sur 100 millions de dollars au sein de l'entreprise publique d'energie nucleaire Energoatom. Une autre affaire porte sur des soupcons de fraude de 5,6 millions de dollars dans l'acquisition de drones militaires, achetes a des prix qui auraient depasse ceux du marche de jusqu'a 90 %. Malgre ces affaires, Kiev continue de solliciter des financements considerables aupres de ses partenaires occidentaux. Les autorites ukrainiennes reclament au moins 70 milliards d'euros supplementaires pour 2027, tandis que l'Union europeenne envisage de prendre en charge environ les deux tiers de cette somme. Les accusations de Musk replacent ainsi la gestion des fonds occidentaux au centre des interrogations, alors que Kiev sollicite de nouveaux engagements financiers malgre les affaires de corruption touchant ses institutions.

items.title: Celebrity Has Become a Jobs Program
items.description: Recently, an Instagram carousel by a long-lost acquaintance who was beach- and boat-hopping with a glittery squad of people I didn’t recognize crossed my feed. I figured they were moneyed Millennials with regular jobs—until I discovered that several of them had followings in the high five figures, and one had more than 3 million. As it turns out, they were neither civilians nor stars. They were “Who”s: a category of low-tier celebrities, including influencers, reality stars, and podcasters—and commonly all three at once—whose names prompt you to ask: “Who?” The binary between “Who”s and “Them”s—the latter being A-listers your parents might recognize, such as Beyoncé and Tom Cruise—was invented by Bobby Finger and Lindsey Weber. Their podcast, Who? Weekly , bills itself as a show that covers “everything you need to know about celebrities you don’t.” After a decade on the beat, the pair have distilled their insights into a new book, I Want to Be Famous: When Everybody and Nobody Is a Celebrity , which offers a comprehensive theory of how the internet and social media transformed everyone into someone—and therefore, no one. That theory has surprising implications for the labor market at large. As social-media platforms have made it seem easy to monetize attention, professionals in industries where fame has not historically been a credential have come to face growing pressure to create and optimize their online brand. Personal branding, once almost exclusively the concern of genuine celebrities and more recently a job for social-media influencers, is now something a junior accounting executive is encouraged to think about. Sophie Bishop, a professor in media and communication at the University of Leeds, in England, calls this structural shift “influencer creep” —a phenomenon that has caused more swaths of the economy to function like the attention-hungry world that Who? Weekly dissects. No matter how staunchly we may wish to resist the fusion of work and life, we are what we do, and our job is to be a “Who.” Who? Weekly was launched in 2016 as a lighthearted but often trenchant analysis of fame at a time when social media was beginning to democratize the concept. Finger and Weber were both young entertainment journalists; as they write in I Want to Be Famous , they wanted a venue in which to grumble about celebrities turning away from traditional media and toward social platforms, where they could exercise more image control. Finger and Weber’s real innovation, however, was the system of Whos and Thems. Whos are thirsty for the attention that Thems already have and will shamelessly do or plug anything to get it. “By the end of the 2010s,” the authors write, “it seemed like every reality star, aspiring actor or musician, and TikTok influencer was supplementing their creative income with a post promoting a vibrator, supplement, gambling service, or alcoholic beverage.” [ Read more: The celebrity clock is getting rewired ] But as I Want to Be Famous reveals, social-media culture has changed so much that even Thems can no longer resist shilling for brands online. When Jennifer Aniston joined Instagram, in 2019, her first post was a selfie with her Friends co-stars. “It was a charming (if brief) glimpse into the personal life of one of our most private celebrities,” Finger and Weber write: “The purity of her feed was short-lived, however. Today, you can see ads for SkinnyPop popcorn among those intimate photos with friends because now everyone is free to sell stuff in this brave new world, without the fear of selling out.” Last month, another Them joined Instagram: the Oscar-winning actor Jennifer Lawrence, who in a video warned fans to be nice, or she’d quit. A couple of weeks later, Lawrence posted a carousel with grainy photos that were, in part, normal-person coded: There she was, eating a corn dog and riding the Tower of Terror. Except she was also at a Dior fashion show in Paris—right, she’s a movie star. “Thank you @dior and @jonathan.anderson for the most beautiful show ever,” she wrote in the caption. Maybe Lawrence joined the platform for the same reasons we all did: to make internet friends jealous with vacation pics. Or maybe her long-running role as a brand ambassador for Dior now requires her to broker attention online. We can’t know why anyone posts anything: for love or money, connection or commerce. But last week, Lawrence shared low-res, behind-the-scenes snapshots of her hairstyles in various movies, and updated her Instagram bio with a link to her new hair-care brand. [ Read more: The celebrity machine never dies ] Who? Weekly chronicles the rise of online attention and the decline of offline mystique. A 2024 post on the Harvard Business School blog offers an example. Branding yourself as a “financial analyst with high emotional intelligence who loves to ski,” the author argues, can help you find opportunities “that align with your authentic self.” The post also suggests that a job seeker might “promote your value” by using “a mix of paid, owned, and earned media.” What this means is that, to really get your mug in front of hiring managers and corporate recruiters, you should pay to amplify material that communicates your professional viability. Some Gen Z job seekers are using Instagram and TikTok to pitch themselves to potential employers. A 2025 survey found that 46 percent of Gen Z respondents had landed a job or an internship through TikTok. And LinkedIn, once a straitlaced professional networking site, now also functions something like Instagram for the corporate class. The idea is that becoming a platform personality through personal posts or videos will juice the algorithm and thus woo recruiters. The rise of the LinkedInfluencer is emblematic of the act of self-promotion becoming more front-facing: As Brooke Erin Duffy, a communication professor at Cornell University, asked in a June interview with The New York Times , “What does it mean for the rest of us who are living, working and spending our time in these sites where everything we see has this ethos of self promotion?” Companies including Starbucks and IBM have launched so-called employee-creator programs, initiatives that offers everyday workers rewards for serving as in-house posters. “We’re giving them a way to become influencers,” a July press release by Gap Inc. boasted about one such initiative. But the imperative to build followers stretches across corporate tiers. Jon Gray, the president and chief operating officer of Blackstone —one of the largest commercial landlords in the world—has gone viral on LinkedIn with relatably goofy videos of himself running; the platform’s editor in chief and vice president of content, Dan Roth, recently bragged that Gray has “become a creator.” How odd to feel sympathy for a billionaire: Somehow, he too is furiously—literally—running on the content hamster wheel. [ Read more: So a C-list celebrity is selling your house? ] Finger and Weber point out that, until recently, a professional working for a major corporation could count on a fairly linear career path. The same wasn’t true for someone like a reality star, who needed to rely on media access to sustain their fame and find new opportunities; they might start a lifestyle brand, for instance, in service of becoming what the authors call a “working Who.” Plenty of jobs don’t appear to be succumbing to this shift, at least not yet; your Instagram algorithm might surface the odd plumbing influencer, but your leaky faucet is unlikely to get fixed under the flattering glare of a ring light. Influencer culture has gone only so far in reshaping the labor market in its image, but as the corporate world adopts its practices, there is a growing incentive for you to become your own kind of “working Who”—and, in turn, to help reinforce the idea that people are products.

items.title: Pourvoyeuse d’époux (Le billet de Ndiol Maka SECK)
items.description: Pour ceux qui ne remplissent pas les critères pour décrocher le très convoité poste de « mari » de tata Ndella, inutile de ranger définitivement les costumes au placard. Tout espoir n’est pas perdu ! La « tata nationale » vient de lancer un nouvel appel à candidatures. Que les mauvaises langues se rassurent : le premier n’a pas été un échec. Bien au contraire, tata Ndella croule sous les dossiers au point de ne plus savoir à quel prétendant donner la priorité. Dans une vidéo devenue virale, elle a confié avoir du mal à gérer cette montagne de candidatures. Mais pendant que les prétendants attendent le verdict, l’ancienne patronne de « Keur Yeurmandé » a décidé de jouer les entremetteuses pour sa propre fille. Une maman reste une maman ! Dans une publication, elle a lancé cet appel pour le moins direct : « Qui veut épouser ma fille ? Elle a 34 ans demain, le 22 octobre (aujourd’hui). Elle est très gentille… ». Mais attention, une question demeure : cette initiative bénéficie-t-elle de l’accord de celle à qui le fameux mari est destiné ? Dans cette affaire, il semble qu’il ne suffit pas d’avoir un bon dossier. Prudence donc pour éviter des complications futures dans l’intimité conjugale ! ndiolmaka.seck@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Accident de la circulation sur l’axe Ndande-Kébémer : le ministre des Transports au chevet des victimes à Louga
items.description: Au lendemain du tragique accident survenu vendredi soir sur l’axe Ndande-Kébémer, qui a fait plusieurs morts et blessés, le ministre des Transports terrestres et aériens, Abdou Lahad Ndiaye, s’est rendu, ce samedi, à l’hôpital régional Amadou Sakhir Mbaye de Louga pour s’enquérir de la situation des victimes. Cette visite a été l’occasion pour le ministre d’apporter son soutien moral aux blessés et de leur témoigner sa compassion en ces moments douloureux. Sur place, Abdou Lahad Ndiaye a salué le professionnalisme du personnel de santé mobilisé pour la prise en charge des victimes. Selon lui, les équipes médicales mettent tout en œuvre pour sauver les blessés. Par ailleurs, le bilan de l’accident s’est alourdi, passant de six à huit morts. Cette nouvelle tragédie relance la question de la recrudescence des accidents de la circulation et de leurs lourdes conséquences humaines. Elle souligne l’urgence de renforcer les mesures de prévention et de sécurité routière afin de réduire les risques d’accident et de préserver les vies humaines. Falel PAM

items.title: GH¢49.72m S.A. evacuation: Some evacuees didn’t receive reintegration and transport allowance – JoyNews Research
items.description: JoyNews Research has found that some of the 1,964 Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa did not receive their GH¢5,000 reintegration allowance and GH¢500 transport allowance, despite the government spending GH¢49.72 million on the exercise. Head of Research at JoyNews, Isaac Kofi Adjei, disclosed this on JoyNews Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, while outlining findings from the team’s independent analysis of data relating to the evacuation. He said the team’s checks also uncovered duplicate names in the records, payments without signatures and expenditure for which supporting receipts were unavailable. “So after our independent analysis, we built a system to actually test this data. We manually also checked all the numbers that we had received and we came out with at least five conclusions that the data that we had did not support so many claims that were made by the Foreign Affairs Minister,” he said. Mr Adjei explained that the team tested the list of 1,964 evacuees subsequently shared by the Foreign Affairs Minister and found discrepancies in the records it had analysed. “When we did our checks, we realised there were duplicates in terms of names in the document that we had received and we had analysed. We also saw that some of the evacuees received monies, but there were no signatures. “And there were those who did not receive the 5,000 resettlement allowance or reintegration allowance and the 500 cedis transport allowance,” he said. The findings also included records containing dates of birth that appeared to be in the future or were otherwise impossible. Mr Adjei said the Foreign Affairs Ministry or Ghana’s mission in Pretoria subsequently provided clarification on that issue. Another concern was the absence of receipts for some expenditure items included in the government’s response to Parliament and in data obtained by JoyNews Research. Mr Adjei cited accommodation and transportation expenses incurred in South Africa as examples of expenditure for which the team had not received receipts. “We also have transport expenses in South Africa; we didn’t have receipts for that and other expenses,” he said. He stressed that the findings emerged from the team’s initial checks of the data obtained from its sources, adding that JoyNews Research had also examined data collected directly by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs during the evacuation. “And I think subsequently we were finished with the primary data if I should say that or the original data that the ministry itself collected on the day. We have done that check as well. And Monday we are airing the findings here on Joy News,” he said.

items.title: The Temporary Pleasure of Conversation
items.description: This is an edition of The Wonder Reader, a newsletter in which our editors recommend a set of stories to spark your curiosity and fill you with delight. Sign up here to get it every Saturday morning. Conversation, Charlie Tyson wrote in 2023, is by nature fleeting. He quotes Virginia Woolf: “It flies up the chimney,” she once said, “and is gone.” This perspective may be comforting for people who spend hours after a social interaction perseverating over that one joke that didn’t quite land. But Woolf’s remark doesn’t necessarily imply that conversation is meaningless. Understanding that conversations are temporary, that they fly up the chimney to make room for new ones, can help us talk to one another more honestly. “In the twists of talk, we open ourselves to others and allow our interior to be subtly reshaped,” Tyson wrote in his review of a book on the subject. The benefits of conversation are constantly threatened by modern life—by the pull of a phone notification during lunch with a friend, by the impulse to text instead of call, and perhaps most dramatically, by AI’s promise to obviate the human need for talking. Woolf’s description of language might make it seem replaceable, but this transient quality is precisely what makes talking an essential part of life. Language is something we are creating, demolishing, and creating again, every second of every day—a distinctly human act. On Conversation The Secret to a Good Conversation By Charlie Tyson A new cultural history embraces talk as an open-ended source of temporary delight. ( From 2023 ) Read the article. The Secret Life of 'Um' By Julie Beck How filler words and tiny pauses keep conversations from going off the rails ( From 2017 ) Read the article. Embrace the Awkward Silence By Michael Waters Conversational lulls may be harder to avoid than ever—so we might as well get used to them. ( From 2023 ) Read the article. Still Curious? How to cheat at conversation : A new AI tool promises to improve social interactions but instead makes them worse, Julie Beck wrote last year. Overcoming awkwardness : In the first episode of our 2023 podcast How to Talk to People , Julie Beck and Becca Rashid discuss small talk. Other Diversions Stop trying to be your best self. 50 unforgettable love stories An anti-marriage marriage movie PS Courtesy of Dorothy B. “Although we usually appreciate the beauty of trees in full leaf, I was stunned by the bare-branched symmetry of this tree on a quiet winter day in our small town,” Dorothy B. from La Conner, Washington, writes. I’ll continue to feature your responses in the coming weeks.

items.title: WPL 2026/27: Hasaacas Ladies claim 2-1 away win over Army Ladies
items.description: Hasaacas Ladies enjoyed a winning start to the 2026/27 GoldFields Women’s Premier League following their victory over Army Ladies. Hasaacas claimed a 2-1 away win over Army in the fixture which was played at the Mats Park in Teshie on Saturday, October 24. The Hasmal Ladies came into the fixture on the back of a 1-0 victory over Ampem Darkoa Ladies in the Champion of Champions, with Raymond Fenny making one change to the team that defeated the league winners last weekend. Hasaacas enjoyed a good spell of possession in the opening 25 minutes of the game but were unable to break the backline of Army. However, they eventually found the breakthrough in the 32nd minute when a howler at the back presented an opportunity to Comfort Owusu, who fed Milot Pokuaa for the first goal of the game. Grace Banwaa made a few saves to deny the home side an equaliser as Hasaacas went into the break with a 1-0 lead. Army came back stronger in the second half of the game, creating a flurry of chances. Their great spell of possession left spaces at the back as Hasaacas won for themselves a penalty which was converted by Belinda Kpoglo to double the away side’s advantage in the 60th minute. Shortly after doubling their lead through the spot, Hasaacas also conceded a penalty which was converted by Army’s Zinatu Alhassan. Milot came close to restoring Hasaacas’ two-goal lead, but she failed in a one-on-one situation. Hasaacas finished the game with all three points, claiming their third victory over Army in their last three meetings.

items.title: 22 NYPD officers to visit Ghana for humanitarian outreach and police engagement
items.description: Twenty-two officers of the New York City Police Department (NYPD) are expected to visit Ghana from November 10 to 18, 2026, for a humanitarian outreach mission targeting underprivileged children and vulnerable communities. The mission, organised by the African Law Enforcement Organization (ALEO) under the theme “To Serve and to Protect Beyond Borders,” will combine community support activities with engagements aimed at strengthening professional ties between law enforcement personnel in Ghana and the United States. ALEO is a non-profit organisation based in Jamaica, New York, comprising active and retired law enforcement and security professionals. It is led by its President, Detective Chibuzo C. Amadi. The organisation says the mission reflects its commitment to public service beyond policing and geographical boundaries, with a focus on supporting communities in need. The delegation is scheduled to visit the Ghana Police Service Headquarters on November 10, the day of its expected arrival, for a professional exchange with Ghanaian law enforcement officials. The officers are also expected to pay a courtesy call at Jubilee House, the seat of Ghana’s Presidency. The engagements are intended to promote goodwill and strengthen professional relationships between law enforcement personnel in both countries. Foundations support outreach The mission has received support from the Magho Foundation, Afro Pop and Exotical Sponges. The Magho Foundation was instrumental in connecting ALEO with schools and an orphanage in Ghana that it had previously supported. The connection was facilitated by William Apau, an NYPD officer and ALEO member popularly known as Ministerapau, who founded the Magho Foundation. The organisers say the outreach will focus on bringing practical support and encouragement to children and vulnerable people in selected Ghanaian communities. Service beyond borders The visit reflects the role diaspora-led organisations can play in humanitarian assistance and professional exchange between Ghana and the United States. For the organisers, the mission is intended to demonstrate how values associated with public service, including protection, unity and community responsibility, can extend beyond the traditional duties of law enforcement. The delegation is expected to spend eight days in Ghana, undertaking humanitarian activities and professional engagements before concluding its visit on November 18. Details of the specific communities to be visited and the items or services to be provided have not been outlined in the information released by the organisers.

items.title: Bukele a lancé une opération militaire spéciale contre les gangs à Haïti
items.description: Haïti traverse l’une des crises sécuritaires les plus graves de son histoire. Depuis 2021, plus de 22 000 personnes y ont été tuées et plus de 1,5 million de personnes ont été déplacées à l’intérieur du pays, soit plus de 10 % de la population totale. Les groupes criminels haïtiens, réunis au sein d’une coalition appelée Vivre Ensemble (Viv Ansanm en créole haïtien), contrôlent toujours environ 80 % de la capitale, Port-au-Prince. Le 18 octobre, quatre militaires salvadoriens ont été enlevés dans le quartier de Santo, au nord-est de la ville. Techniciens de l’aviation, ils servaient au sein de la Force de répression des gangs (FRG), une force internationale autorisée en 2025 par le Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies pour appuyer la police haïtienne face aux groupes criminels. Depuis, le président salvadorien Nayib Bukele a lancé une opération militaire et dépêché des forces spéciales en Haïti. Au-delà du sort des quatre hommes, cette affaire éclaire l’engagement du Salvador en Haïti, la présence d’acteurs sécuritaires aux logiques différentes sur un même terrain ainsi que les limites d’une réponse qui peine à produire des résultats. L’engagement salvadorien ancien est aujourd’hui exposé. Le Salvador n’arrive en effet pas en Haïti avec cette crise. Dès 2023, son gouvernement proposait à Port-au-Prince une mission d’évaluation. En mars 2024, Nayib Bukele affirmait pouvoir « régler » la crise haïtienne, à condition d’obtenir une résolution du Conseil de sécurité, le consentement des autorités haïtiennes et la prise en charge des coûts. En octobre 2024, l’Assemblée salvadorienne a autorisé l’envoi d’un contingent chargé des évacuations médicales au sein de la Mission multinationale d’appui à la sécurité. Ce contingent est arrivé au début de l’année 2025 avec ses hélicoptères. Il a ensuite rejoint la FRG, et le 2 octobre, une loi est entrée en vigueur pour élargir son rôle. Les quatre militaires enlevés appartiennent à cette unité aérienne. Pour Bukele, il s’agit d’une affaire devenue nationale. Le 21 octobre, le président salvadorien a annoncé le lancement d’une opération militaire dans une publication sur X et s’est adressé directement aux chefs de gangs, y compris en créole haïtien. Il a rappelé que ces militaires étaient des techniciens chargés d’évacuations médicales et a prévenu d’une réponse plus forte serait apportée s’ils n’étaient pas libérés vivants. Le lendemain, cent membres des forces spéciales sont arrivés à Port-au-Prince, et un renfort équivalent a été annoncé. Pou chèf gang yo ak manm gang yo k ap kenbe kat konpatriyòt nou yo an otaj ann Ayiti : Mesye nou kidnape yo pa konbatan. Yo se teknisyen nan domèn avyasyon ki fè pati misyon nou ann Ayiti, nan kad yon misyon entènasyonal. Misyon nou an gen sèlman pilòt ak pèsonèl teknik, ki gen… pic.twitter.com/BNKbWTAQQp — Nayib Bukele (@nayibbukele) October 21, 2026 L’affaire est devenue une question de politique intérieure mais aussi personnelle : pour Bukele, il s’agit de montrer que l’État ne laisse pas ses soldats derrière face à des gangs, adversaires sur lesquels le président a bâti son régime et sa stature internationale. Avant de prétendre peser sur le terrain haïtien, ce message s’adresse autant à l’opinion salvadorienne qu’à ses interlocuteurs étrangers, en premier lieu l’administration Trump. Les modalités de ce renfort restent pourtant floues. La FRG a confirmé son arrivée sans préciser comment elle s’intègre à ses opérations. Lorsqu’un pays qui contribue déjà à la force déploie des unités en parallèle, il est légitime de se demander si les cadres multilatéral et national commencent à se superposer, et comment la coordination sera assurée. Jusqu’ici, le calendrier de la FRG était dicté par la logistique et les négociations politiques. Le processus était lent, mais il avançait. Cette crise le fait voler en éclats. La force, dont le déploiement reste incomplet, se retrouve ainsi dans une posture réactive, prise dans un piège tactique. Dans le quartier de Santo, elle opère aux côtés de la police haïtienne, mais aussi et surtout aux côtés de sa propre Task Force. Au sein de cette dernière opère, de manière assez opaque, la société militaire privée Vectus Global d’ Erik Prince , qui conduit des frappes de drones en Haïti contre les zones contrôlées par les gangs depuis mars 2025. Tous ces acteurs, y compris les opérateurs de drones, sont engagés dans les opérations à Santo. C’est la première fois que la FRG et Vectus Global opèrent sur le même terrain. La présence simultanée de Bukele et de Prince au cœur des opérations tient aux circonstances. Elle n’est pas pour autant sans antécédents. Erik Prince a rencontré Nayib Bukele en 2024 et s’est fait l’un des promoteurs du modèle sécuritaire salvadorien ; Vectus Global emploie des Salvadoriens en Haïti. Ce brouillage des rôles entre acteurs multilatéraux, nationaux et sociétés militaires privées soulève des questions de responsabilité et de règles d’engagement qui ne sont absolument pas tranchées ou documentées pour le moment. Il met aussi les forces de sécurité face à leurs limites. Pour la FRG, le gouvernement et la police, l’incident fait peser un risque d’embarras majeur : plus il se prolonge, plus il fragilise chacun d’eux. Après cinq jours d’opérations, aucun progrès n’est visible, et aucune information officielle n’a été communiquée sur le sort des otages ou d’éventuelles négociations. Opérer au cœur d’un territoire contrôlé par les gangs est une épreuve redoutable, que les forces de sécurité ne semblent pas en mesure de surmonter pleinement. Au-delà des questions de formation et de coordination, le principal déficit tient au renseignement. Les forces nationales et internationales manquent d’informations fiables, zone par zone et groupe par groupe, ainsi que de moyens pour les protéger et de les partager en sécurité. Ce manque pèse d’autant plus dans une crise comme celle-ci. Pour les groupes criminels, il s’agit d’un levier dont Santo montre les limites. Viv Ansanm montrait ces derniers mois des signes de fragmentation ; cet incident pourrait restaurer sa cohésion. Cette coalition fédère depuis 2024 les principaux gangs de la capitale. Ses attaques ont précipité la chute du gouvernement d’Ariel Henry, et les États-Unis l’ont désignée comme organisation terroriste en 2025. Deux de ses chefs les plus importants ont pris la parole cette semaine. Krisla, qui contrôle Carrefour, a mis en garde les forces salvadoriennes, tandis que Lanmò San Jou s’est dit prêt à se battre. Si les tons diffèrent, le message converge et montre que ces groupes entendent tenir leur terrain, et la bataille de la communication sur les réseaux sociaux est ouverte. Détenir des militaires place aussi les gangs dans une logique de prise d’otages, et pas seulement de kidnappings contre rançon, l’une de leurs spécialités. Les captifs deviennent alors une monnaie d’échange, un moyen de pression, mais aussi peut-être, un bouclier. Santo montre cependant les limites de ce calcul. Les otages n’ont en effet pas arrêté ni les opérations au sol ni les frappes de drones, et le coût pourrait retomber sur les civils. Santo est un territoire contrôlé par les gangs Chen Mechan et 400 Mawozo, mais ce n’est pas là que leurs chefs sont basés. Qui, dès lors, est visé ? Des membres de gangs figurent parmi les victimes, mais les témoignages d’habitants pris au piège décrivent un véritable déluge de feu, avec peu d’informations sur les mesures de protection prévues pour eux. La nouveauté la plus significative est que la sécurité haïtienne produit des effets à l’étranger. Ces dernières années, malgré un engagement international et multilatéral constant, les drames haïtiens, à commencer par les massacres, ont rarement eu de réelles conséquences politiques, en Haïti comme à l’étranger. Les exceptions tenaient aux crises politiques, comme la fin du mandat du Conseil présidentiel de transition en février, qui avait suscité des réactions extérieures, dont le déploiement d’un navire de guerre américain. Cette fois, tous les fils se rejoignent dans le champ politique. La crise place le gouvernement haïtien sous une forte pression intérieure, expose la FRG et les pays qui y contribuent, et pourrait peser sur les décisions des bailleurs de fonds comme des pays appelés à déployer des troupes. Les résultats sécuritaires ont désormais un coût politique, à Port-au-Prince comme dans les capitales qui soutiennent la force. Cela va marquer sans aucun doute la période qui s’ouvre. L’article Bukele a lancé une opération militaire spéciale contre les gangs à Haïti est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Ajax : Abdellah Ouazane dans le viseur de plusieurs cadors européens
items.description: Abdellah Ouazane serait dans le viseur de plusieurs cadors européens, dont Chelsea, Manchester City, le Real Madrid et la Juventus. Lié au club néerlandais jusqu’en juin 2028, le Lionceau de l’Atlas suscite un intérêt grandissant sur le marché des transferts. Abdellah Ouazane pourrait bientôt se retrouver au cœur d’une bataille entre plusieurs grands clubs européens. Selon les informations relayées par le journaliste Ekrem Konur, le jeune milieu de terrain de l’Ajax Amsterdam serait suivi par Chelsea, Manchester City, le Real Madrid et la Juventus. Âgé de 17 ans, le joueur marocain figure parmi les jeunes talents à surveiller dans le football européen. Son profil attire l’attention de formations prestigieuses, même si aucun transfert ni aucune négociation concrète n’ont été confirmés à ce stade. Formé au sein du club amstellodamois, Abdellah Ouazane est lié à l’Ajax jusqu’en juin 2028. Cette situation contractuelle place le club néerlandais en position favorable face aux éventuels prétendants, qui devraient passer par lui pour envisager un recrutement. Pour l’Ajax, l’enjeu sera de poursuivre le développement de son jeune joueur tout en résistant à l’intérêt que pourrait susciter son potentiel auprès des grandes écuries européennes. L’intérêt annoncé de Chelsea, Manchester City, du Real Madrid et de la Juventus reste donc à suivre. Les prochains mois permettront de mesurer si cette attention se transforme en démarches concrètes ou si l’Ajax parvient à conserver l’un de ses jeunes talents. The post Ajax : Abdellah Ouazane dans le viseur de plusieurs cadors européens appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Bawumia meets Ghana Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists to discuss healthcare reforms
items.description: New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has held consultations with the leadership of the Ghana Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists (GAMLS) on policy proposals to strengthen Ghana’s healthcare system. The discussions covered the proposed establishment of a dedicated regulatory council for medical laboratory science, financial clearance for the recruitment of health professionals, local production of laboratory reagents, stronger disease surveillance systems and strategic partnerships with the private sector. Dr Bawumia said the engagement provided an opportunity to exchange ideas on challenges facing the health sector and explore practical measures to improve healthcare delivery. Medical laboratory services play a central role in disease diagnosis, treatment decisions and the detection of public health threats. Improving staffing, access to laboratory supplies and professional regulation could therefore affect the quality and reliability of services across the country. The proposed local production of laboratory reagents also featured among the issues discussed, amid the broader need to strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity and reduce reliance on imported diagnostic supplies. Dr Bawumia expressed gratitude to GAMLS leadership and members for sharing their perspectives, reiterating his commitment to developing policies informed by stakeholder engagement and the experiences of Ghanaians. The consultation forms part of his engagements with professional groups on priorities for the country’s healthcare sector. The proposals would require further policy development, including details on the proposed regulatory council, recruitment arrangements and measures to support local reagent production. For medical laboratory scientists, the issues extend beyond professional regulation and working conditions to the wider capacity of Ghana’s health system to deliver accurate diagnoses, monitor disease outbreaks and respond to emerging public health threats.

items.title: Jordan king orders 'iron fist' response to deadly church attack
items.description: Jordan’s King Abdullah ordered security forces on Saturday to respond with an “iron fist” as authorities searched for gunmen who opened fire and killed nine people during a church funeral service. The assailants fired for several minutes in broad daylight at the church in Karak governorate on Friday, and also wounded 40 people in the rare attack on Jordan’s Christian minority. Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across the country, the US embassy in Amman said. A priest described how he and others ordered people to get to the ground at Saint George’s Greek Orthodox church, about 120km (75 miles) southwest of the capital, Amman. “A sense of panic took hold among those present,” Theodoros Soueiss told Reuters . “The gunfire was indiscriminate, and you never knew where a bullet might land.” King Abdullah condemned the “despicable terrorist act” as he chaired a National Security Council meeting and said there was no room for leniency when it comes to the lives of Jordanians, the royal court said. Such attacks are highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack in the kingdom, a major partner with the US in the fight against militant groups. Officials have said it is too early to determine whether the attackers had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. “A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word,” said Tarek Ammarin at a hospital where the wounded were being treated. A relative of Ammarin’s was injured in the attack. Christians make up a minority of Jordan’s population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world. Jordan has been among the US allies in the Middle East to be hit by Iranian attacks this year after the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February. Bahjat al-Rushda, mayor of Shihan village in Karak, joined a long list of officials condemning what they called an attack by extremist terrorists. “God willing, this country will remain secure,” he said.

items.title: Air Algérie : 5 nouvelles lignes dont Lagos et Shanghai, leurs dates de lancement
items.description: Air Algérie continue d’étoffer son réseau international, avec le lancement de cinq nouvelles lignes vers des destinations en Afrique et en Asie. La part du lion revient au continent africain où la compagnie aérienne nationale ne cesse de renforcer ses positions afin de faire de l’aéroport d’Alger un hub avec les autres continents. Dans ce cadre, Air Algérie a annoncé ce samedi 24 octobre le « lancement de cinq nouvelles destinations internationales à destination de Conakry, Brazzaville, Lagos, Shanghai et Tripoli ». Ces cinq nouvelles lignes ont été lancées dans le cadre de la « poursuite du développement de son réseau international et du renforcement de la connectivité aérienne, en cohérence avec les efforts de l'État visant à développer le secteur du transport aérien et à répondre aux besoins de sa clientèle et des opérateurs économiques », explique Air Algérie. Air Algérie : le programme de lancement des cinq nouvelles lignes La compagnie aérienne nationale a également dévoilé le programme de lancement des cinq nouvelles liaisons aériennes : Alger – Conakry : 25 octobre 2026 Alger – Brazzaville : 26 octobre 2026 Alger – Lagos : 26 octobre 2026 Alger – Shanghai : 26 octobre 2026 Alger – Tripoli : 28 octobre 2026 L'ouverture de ces liaisons vient renforcer le « maillage du réseau aérien » de la compagnie aérienne nationale sur le continent africain et accompagner « l'ouverture de l'Algérie sur son environnement continental, en élargissant les possibilités de déplacement, en développant les perspectives d'échanges économiques et commerciaux et en consolidant les liens avec les pays africains. » Air Algérie : trois lignes aériennes vers la Chine Pour la ligne Alger-Shanghai, elle vient « étendre la desserte du marché chinois » par Air Algérie, en complément des liaisons vers Pékin et Guangzhou. Cette nouvelle desserte, qui porte à trois le nombre de villes chinoises desservies par Air Algérie, offre des « possibilités supplémentaires de déplacement vers l'un des principaux pôles économiques et commerciaux de Chine ». Elle ouvre aussi des « perspectives plus larges pour les échanges et les activités économiques entre les deux pays. » Enfin, Air Algérie explique que le lancement de ces cinq nouvelles destinations s'inscrit dans sa stratégie visant à « diversifier son réseau de lignes internationales et à élargir son offre de transport aérien, afin de renforcer la connectivité entre l'Algérie et son environnement régional et international, tout en étendant la présence du Groupe sur de nouveaux marchés. » L’article Air Algérie : 5 nouvelles lignes dont Lagos et Shanghai, leurs dates de lancement est apparu en premier sur TSA .

Road infrastructure encroachment fuels pedestrian knockdowns
items.description: The increasing encroachment on road pavements and other infrastructure by petty traders and hawkers within the Greater Accra Metropolitan Area and other large cities continues to raise road safety concerns, prompting the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) to start a stakeholder engagement to address the menace. While malfunctioning traffic lights, broken road signs, faded road markings and bad driver behaviour are driving road crashes and deaths, the situation has been worsened by petty traders who obstruct pedestrian walkways by displaying their merchandise. For over a year now, the Daily Graphic has observed that some traders display their wares on pavements designated as pedestrian walkways, while others pitch camps at bus stops, forcing drivers to park their vehicles on the shoulders of roads. In some cases, the drivers park their vehicles on both sides of roads, a development that impedes vehicular movement, creates human traffic and puts pedestrians in danger. The Central Business District of Accra is bursting with such encroachments; the Mallam Market area and the Kaneshie enclave on the Dr Busia Highway, areas around the Kwame Nkrumah Interchange, as well as Kwabenya to the Achimota Mall are among the areas where the encroachments are rife, leaving city guards and police personnel overwhelmed. Some of the other areas in Accra that have gained notoriety for the encroachment on road infrastructure by petty traders include Odorkor Tipper to the main traffic light, Madina, Nima-Mamobi, and Agbogbloshie. The Graphic Road, which stretches from the intersection at the Farisco Traffic Light on the Kwame Nkrumah Avenue to the Obistebi Lamptey Interchange, is also notorious for the encroachment on road pavements, with a new entrant emerging every day. Between the Graphic Road overpass, near the Graphic Head Office, up to the Farisco Traffic Light is the epicentre for the illegal trading activities on that street. Traders display their wares on the pavements and portions of the road leading from the Accra Brewery to the Graphic Press House with impunity, and the activity starts from about 8 p.m. and continues to the wee hours of the following day. The encroachments, which started from one end of the dual carriageway, have not only become widespread with many traders joining the fray, but both sides of the road pavements are under siege. To facilitate traffic flow, the police have had to station their men to direct traffic, as commercial vehicles are also cashing in on the presence of traders and shoppers right on the road. The joint activities of traders, buyers and commercial vehicles have created chaotic situations, as drivers stop in the middle of the road to load, while illegal and wanton U-turns have also emerged with impunity. Commercial drivers park their vehicles on both sides of the road beyond the Graphic Press House to the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) area as they wait for passengers to board them. Pedestrians are left vulnerable as they have to weave their way through a sea of vehicles that run bumper to bumper, while personnel from the Motor Traffic and Transport Division (MTTD) of the Ghana Police direct traffic. Experiences A driver of a minibus that plies Accra-Kaneshie, Daniel Obeng, explained to the Daily Graphic that he parked his vehicle on the shoulders of the road around the Graphic House because the bus stop had been encroached upon by traders. “Drivers are supposed to stop at bus stops to load our cars, but the bus stops are now used by traders for commercial activities and that is why we also park on the shoulders of the road to get passengers,” he said. A 39-year-old cassava dough seller, Yaa Ntreh, complained that she and other traders displayed their wares on the pavements at the Graphic Press House because the CBD was choked. “We cannot find space at the CBD to sell our wares, so we decided to sell here. Also, where we are now is strategic; people can easily locate us and buy our goods,” she said. In the wake of the lawlessness of the traders and drivers, pedestrians remain vulnerable to road crashes. “If you are walking from Accra Brewery side towards the COCOBOD road and you are not very careful, drivers can just knock you down. You cannot walk on the pavement because it has been taken over by traders,” 27-year-old Adamu Rufai, a shopper, said. The Daily Graphic observed that at Agbogbloshie, Nima-Mamobi and the Odorkor Tipper, petty traders have taken over pavements leading to the main traffic lights with yams, furniture, wood products and other merchandise. At the same time, articulated trucks have been parked on both sides of the major road at these places, making the spaces narrow for vehicles to move freely. Pedestrian knockdowns Encroachment on the road infrastructure is problematic because it results in pedestrian knockdowns, which account for 33 per cent of deaths from reported road crashes, according to the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA). The Daily Graphic’s analysis of road traffic statistics from the NRSA revealed that over the past 35 years (1991 to 2025), 63,599 persons died from reported road crashes across the country, with about 20,988 of those deaths resulting from pedestrian knockdowns. Law on trading on pavements The new Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519) and Road Traffic (Amendment) Act, 2025 (Act 1153) outline several prohibitions designed to keep pavements and vehicular roadways clear of informal commercial activities, hawking and unauthorised vending. Regulation 142 (Selling Goods on Roads and Pedestrian Walkways) declares it an explicit offence to “sell, display, offer for sale or deliver goods on or alongside a road, on a pedestrian walkway, near a railway crossing, under a blind-corner sign or within an intersection.” For hawking or selling on roads and walkways, Regulation 142 states that offenders caught displaying, selling or delivering goods on roadsides or pedestrian pathways face “a fine of up to 50 penalty units (approximately GH¢600), imprisonment for as long as three months, or both.” When the Daily Graphic spoke to the Director-General of the NRSA, Abraham Amaliba, on how to deal with the encroachment on roads, he said the authority had started engaging key stakeholders to tackle the menace. For instance, he said the NRSA had held a meeting with the Ghana Highway Authority (GHA), the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service and actors in the road sector to help stem the tide. Again, he said the NRSA had held a meeting with all 29 Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) in the Greater Accra Region to devise a comprehensive strategy to clear encroachers off the streets. “Then also, when you trade on the pavement, it moves the pedestrian back onto the road to compete with vehicles and that leads to pedestrian knockdowns and deaths,” he said. Police action The Director of Education, Research and Training at the police MTTD, Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Alexander Kwaku Obeng, said road safety was about enforcement and the police needed the support of other stakeholders to succeed in enforcing road safety regulations. “If road markings are faded, it will be difficult for the police to enforce the law in that regard; this is why we are happy that there are plans to upgrade roads and incorporate more road markings,” he said. ACP Obeng also said MMDAs needed to rise to their responsibility of decongesting the roads by taking traders off the pavements. He stressed that while the police were willing to enforce the law on traders on the pedestrian walkways, political interference made it difficult. “Enforcement of road traffic regulations had been the weakest link over the years because of human involvement. The use of technology is what is doing the magic and that is what we should do more,” he said. ACP Obeng also said police enforcement of road traffic regulations through digital means was also focused on tackling speeding by drivers since that was the foundation of many crashes.

items.title: Libertés, économie et ordre public (Par Aly DIOUF)
items.description: En France, la mobilisation du samedi 17 octobre 2026, portée notamment par la colère contre la vie chère et les revendications des lycéens et des étudiants, a dégénéré en violences dans plusieurs grandes villes. Selon les médias locaux, les organisateurs ont revendiqué 800.000 manifestants, contre 550.000 d’après le ministère de l’Intérieur. Derrière cette mobilisation sociale d’ampleur, des groupes violents ont multiplié les pillages, les agressions et les dégradations. À Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Bordeaux et Limoges, des commerces ont été saccagés, des bâtiments publics attaqués et des institutions prises pour cible. Les médias rapportent près de 2.400 interpellations et 997 policiers, gendarmes et pompiers blessés. Les conséquences sont également économiques, avec des pertes pour les commerçants, des dégâts sur les équipements publics et des dépenses de remise en état qui pèsent sur les collectivités territoriales. La France est à six mois de l’élection présidentielle ; et naturellement sa classe politique s’est prononcée sur ces évènements. Le Rassemblement national de Marine Le Pen accuse l’exécutif d’impuissance et entend incarner le camp de l’ordre. Bruno Retailleau réclame une réponse plus ferme. Jean-Luc Mélenchon dénonce la gestion gouvernementale des crises sociales. Le chef de l’État, Emmanuel Macron, parle d’« actes pour faire tomber la République ». Il accuse l'ultra gauche et dit que « la main de l’État ne doit pas trembler ». Tout en reconnaissant l’angoisse de la jeunesse, il a demandé au Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu d’engager des consultations avec les syndicats, les partis et les organisations professionnelles. Ici au Sénégal, où les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (Joj) doivent débuter dans moins de dix jours, le Front syndical pour la défense des travailleurs (Fsdt) a observé une grève générale les 21, 22 et 23 octobre 2026 pour dénoncer la dégradation du pouvoir d’achat, la précarisation de l’emploi et le non-respect des engagements pris avec les partenaires sociaux. À la veille de la grève, plusieurs ministres ont fait face à la presse pour faire le point sur la question. Le Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo a proposé un moratoire de trois mois pour favoriser une trêve sociale. Le ministre Mamadou Lamine Dianté a averti que les grévistes pourraient subir des retenues sur salaire et des sanctions disciplinaires. L’exécutif souligne que le préavis déposé ne couvre pas l’ensemble des secteurs concernés. Toutefois, il assure néanmoins rester disponible pour négocier. L’opposition réclame des concertations urgentes et sincères. Une prise de position qui traduit une volonté de transformer la crise sociale en argument politique contre l’exécutif. Babacar Gaye, ancien ministre libéral, est catégorique. Récemment sur un plateau télé, il a affirmé que « derrière tout trouble syndical, il y a une main politique (…). Les syndicalistes ne doivent pas prêter le flanc. Ils doivent discuter avec les autorités et éviter au Sénégal un chaos ». L’un dans l’autre, ces épisodes me font penser à des échanges que j’ai eus avec un confrère d’Asie du Sud-Est, on ne peut plus francophile. « Il y a quelque chose de remarquable en France et dans ses anciennes colonies, en particulier le Sénégal. Vous avez plus ou moins les mêmes problèmes. Vous mettez trop l’accent sur la démocratie et les libertés au point d’hypothéquer l’entrepreneuriat et l’économie », m’a-t-il dit. Je commence à croire sérieusement à ses propos. aly.diouf@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Israeli forces displace families, demolish buildings in occupied West Bank's Hebron
items.description: Israeli forces pushed into the occupied West Bank city of Hebron on Saturday and displaced around 250 families, some in the middle of the night, vowing to exact a heavy price for a deadly attack on soldiers . The Palestinian Authority called for international pressure on Israel to protect residents, who said soldiers announced the evacuations over loudspeakers late at night as they packed what they could and left. Days before tight elections , Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he was planning an operation on a scale not seen since Israel first occupied the West Bank in 1967, after Palestinian fighters killed two Israeli soldiers on Friday at a checkpoint. In the Hebron neighbourhood of Ein Deir Baha, nestled between two hills, vacated buildings were marked by X’s and the streets were deserted, save a pair of Israeli military vehicles. Israeli flags were draped on a house on the slope apparently taken over by troops. Palestinian homes marked with an “X” by the Israeli army after evacuation are seen in Hebron, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Oct 24, 2026. — Reuters Higazi Shawer al-Tamimi, 70, a shopkeeper who sells live chickens and feed and plays a leadership role in the neighbourhood, said he was awakened at 1:00am by soldiers and a senior officer who said he had to leave. “I asked them how long the evacuation would last. They said: ‘Until further notice.’” He told AFP he had only a short time to pack, adding that for some residents, getting out of the neighbourhood was an ordeal. “For example, my wife’s mother, who is 90 years old and lives in the area, had to be carried out because she is ill,” he said. Visiting Hebron, Netanyahu said he and Defence Minister Israel Katz were “considering a very extensive IDF operation in Judea and Samaria, such as has not been carried out since” the 1967 war. The first step would see Israeli forces “enter the neighbourhood from which the terrorists came, evacuate the residents, go from house to house, and destroy the terrorist infrastructure”, he claimed. The Palestinian Authority said it was mobilising its diplomats to seek “urgent international action that goes beyond condemnation” to prevent forced displacement. Hamas, while not claiming credit, hailed Friday’s attack on soldiers and called on supporters to carry out more. ‘Why should I be displaced?’ To Tamimi, this is only happening because Netanyahu wants to win the election on “the blood of the Palestinian people”. He said people were not going anywhere. “I have lived through all the stages of the occupation, and I will die here.” Israeli forces have already demolished some buildings in the immediate vicinity of where the attack took place, and the Tamimis said they did not know if their homes would meet the same fate. Tamimi’s brother, Khaled Shawer al-Tamimi, 68, was staying with his son after the evacuation order. “The army was announcing through loudspeakers: ‘Leave the area.’ So we left.” Higazi Shawer Al Tamimi, 70, who was evicted alongside his family from Ein Deir Baha neighbourhood by Israeli forces, poses for a picture inside his chicken and animal feed shop in Hebron, in the occupied West Bank on Oct 24, 2026. — AFP He told AFP he was surprised to hear Friday’s assailants came from the neighbourhood, which he described as middle-class and law-abiding. “We have never seen or even heard a single gunshot being fired,” he said from his son’s sitting room as children flitted about. “Why should I be displaced from my house?” he continued. The attackers “are the ones who carried out the act, and if the Israeli government wants to punish them, it can punish them.” Hebron governor Khaled Dudin told AFP the army started in the attackers’ neighbourhood, “but there is no guarantee that the operation will not expand”, calling it a form of “collective punishment”. The governor said 150 families had been affected, while Hebron mayor Youssef al-Jaabari and local activist Issa Amro put the figure at 250. Israeli rights group B’Tselem called for urgent international pressure to prevent Israel from pursuing “plans for collective punishment and acts that could constitute war crimes”. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, through a spokesman, voiced concern over Israeli closures that affect Palestinian livelihoods and called for a halt to violence on all sides. Netanyahu promises PA ‘surprise’ The Israeli military said it was “conducting precise, targeted and thorough searches” focused on the area of the two gunmen, who were both killed in a firefight. It added that the operation would last several days. But Netanyahu suggested that bigger action was coming. Asked if he agreed with the idea of dismantling the Palestinian Authority, as has been suggested by his far-right national security minister Itamar Ben Gvir, Netanyahu referred to Israeli military operations in Gaza, Lebanon, Syria and Iran. “We transformed the Middle East,” he said, repeating a common campaign refrain, in an interview with i24News . “There is a very big surprise for the Palestinian Authority as well.” There is no evidence that the Palestinian Authority had any involvement in Friday’s attack. Far-right Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who also holds a position within the defence ministry, called for a large-scale military offensive in the West Bank “ exactly like in Gaza ”. Both Ben Gvir and Smotrich are especially vocal supporters of Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, which have proliferated under Netanyahu’s government but are illegal under international law. Netanyahu has linked the assailants to Hamas, the resistance group in Gaza that carried out the Oct 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest in Israel’s history. The attack came amid rising tensions in the West Bank as Israeli settlers, who enjoy strong support from Netanyahu’s far-right allies, ramp up seizures of Palestinian land and attacks. Rights group Yesh Din reported 672 incidents of settler violence over the past 26 days, nearly half related to the annual olive harvest. According to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry, Israeli forces and settlers have killed 1,117 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the war on Gaza in October 2023. Israeli figures show that at least 51 Israelis, including civilians and security personnel, have been killed in Palestinian attacks or during Israeli military operations during the same period. Polls show Netanyahu is neck and neck with an opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot, a centre-right former military chief who also opposes a Palestinian state but has promised to crack down on settler violence.

items.title: Minority demands Sammy Gyamfi’s resignation as GoldBod CEO over comments on small-scale mining licences
items.description: The Minority Caucus in Parliament has called for the resignation or dismissal of Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi over comments it says suggest that small-scale miners can operate without the requisite licences and permits. The Caucus has also demanded an unqualified apology from Mr Gyamfi, government sanctions against him and a clear roadmap from President John Mahama to end illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. “⁠Mr. Sammy Gyamfi should resign immediately as CEO of GOLDBOD; failing that, he should be dismissed to restore the institution’s credibility,” part of the statement read. “A clear roadmap from President Mahama and his government to end galamsey as promised to Ghanaian prior to the 2024 general elections.” In a statement issued by the Ranking Member of Parliament’s Lands and Natural Resources Committee, Kwaku Ampratwum-Sarpong, the Minority Caucus condemned Mr Gyamfi’s reported position on small-scale mining operations outside restricted areas. The statement questioned the basis for allowing mining without the necessary licences and permits, asking whether such operations could also be permitted in schools, churches, mosques, marketplaces, hospitals, Jubilee House, Parliament and the law courts. “The New Patriotic Party (NPP) calls on Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), other political parties, the Clergy, Traditional Authorities, media houses, the Media Coalition Against Galamsey, the Ghana Chamber of Mines, the Trade Unions, Youth Organisations, Market Women, Professional Bodies, Development Partners, the Diplomatic Community, Concerned Citizens and other well-meaning Ghanaians to condemn Mr Sammy Gyamfi’s reckless comments and the NDC government’s approach to solving galamsey issues contrary to what was promised, and to demand accountability for their stewardship to Ghanaians,” the statement said. The Caucus argued that the position attributed to Mr Gyamfi contradicts the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), particularly Sections 9(1) and 82(1), which provide for licensing requirements for mining activities. It also referred to Section 89 of the Act, which provides for the designation of areas for small-scale mining, insisting that any such arrangement must comply with the law. The Minority Caucus outlined a series of demands, including an apology from Mr Gyamfi and a public condemnation of his remarks by the government, together with appropriate sanctions. The statement further called for a thorough audit of GoldBod’s documentation to establish whether gold purchases can be traced from the mine to the market and whether the purchases comply with responsible-sourcing requirements. “A thorough audit of the Ghana Gold Board’s documentation to verify traceability of all gold purchases, from mine to market to establish responsible sourcing practices.” The Caucus urged President Mahama to present a clear roadmap for ending galamsey and declare a state of emergency in areas it describes as “red flag galamsey hot spots”. It also called for the formalisation of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) through a Legislative Instrument (L.I.). “To declare a state of emergency in all the red flag galamsey hotspots and to formalise the establishment and operations of NAIMOS through an L.I. to give meaning and structure to it.” The Minority Caucus said the demands were necessary to ensure accountability and strengthen efforts to tackle illegal mining.
