items.title: 4 children killed as van plunges into ravine in Neelum Valley
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: Four children were killed and three other people were injured when a van carrying them to a madrasah plunged into a ravine in the upper reaches of Neelum Valley on Saturday, officials said. Neelum Valley District Disaster Management Officer Akhtar Ayoub said the van was travelling from Nagdar, about 22 kilometres from the district headquarters of Athmuqam, via the Keran bypass link road when it plunged into a ravine. “The accident occurred around 8:30am near Ghorray Nakkah Morr in Nagdar, barely half a kilometre into the journey, as the driver negotiated a sharp bend,” he said. The van plunged more than 500 metres off the road into a rocky ravine, killing three children on the spot and initially injuring four other occupants. One of the injured children later died at the District Headquarters Hospital in Athmuqam, Ayoub said. The injured were later shifted to Muzaffarabad for treatment due to their critical condition, he added. Expressing grief over the loss of young lives, Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq extended his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured. “Deeply saddened by the loss of precious young lives in the tragic accident in Neelum Valley today. My heartfelt condolences go out to the bereaved families, and I pray for the speedy recovery of the injured,” he wrote on X. “Mountain roads demand utmost caution; even a momentary lapse can have tragic consequences. Please drive carefully,” he added. A similar accident occurred in April when three people were killed, and 10 others were injured when a passenger van plunged into a deep ravine in the Maidan Nambatai area. On May 11, four people, including two women, were killed and two others injured after a passenger jeep plunged hundreds of feet into a rocky streambed.

items.title: Haris Rauf calls for middle-over breakthroughs as ODI scores soar
items.description: One-day International cricket has gone through changes over the years, but one of the aspects of the game that has continued to be crucial is the importance of taking wickets in the middle overs. In the span of the last three years, which included Pakistan’s dismal 2023 World Cup campaign in India, the national side’s bowlers have struggled to strike as often as they would have liked in the middle overs. Haris Rauf, who has featured for Pakistan in most of the matches through this period, is well aware of the team’s shortcomings as they look forward to the next edition of the World Cup, set to be co-hosted by South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe in 2027. Pakistan’s bowlers have averaged 4.11 dismissals between overs 11 and 40 in ODIs since the start of 2023. The figures underline the challenge facing a side that has often depended on early breakthroughs and late-innings bowling to contain opponents. Speaking to reporters at Gaddafi Stadium on Friday, ahead of Sunday’s tri-series match against England, Haris acknowledged the importance of striking in the middle overs, warning that allowing batters to settle could leave the bowling side struggling to recover. “If you do not take wickets in the middle overs, you will struggle as a team,” the fast bowler said. “If their middle-order batters or openers remain at the crease until the end, they can hurt you.” Pakistan have made a promising start to the ongoing tri-series, beating Sri Lanka by 37 runs and England by 87 in their first two matches. But the contest between England and Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi on Thursday, when the latter chased down a target of 430 after England posted 429-4, offered a reminder of how little room for error bowlers have on batting-friendly surfaces. Haris believes the modern game demands more from both departments, with teams needing to prepare for totals well beyond 300. “Nowadays, we may have to score 350-plus runs ourselves at the World Cup and chase totals of 350-plus as well,” he said. “The support for bowlers is a little less, but you have to keep working on your own skills and make the most of situations when conditions favour you.” One potential source of assistance is reverse swing, particularly with the revised ODI playing conditions introduced in July last year. Under the change, two new balls are used until the end of the 34th over, after which the fielding side chooses one ball to be used at both ends for overs 35 to 50. Previously, a separate ball was used from each end throughout the innings, limiting the extent to which either could age. Haris said the older ball could offer an advantage during daytime matches, when conditions were more conducive to reverse swing, but added that dew could reduce its effectiveness in night games. The opportunity, however, is not enough on its own. Pakistan must translate any assistance into wickets, particularly during the middle overs, when established batters can accelerate and put the bowling attack under pressure. Haris’ own recent domestic performances suggest that he has been working towards greater consistency and endurance. The 32-year-old represented Pakistan Television in four matches of the ongoing President’s Trophy Grade-I competition, taking 18 wickets, averaging 20.11, including two four-wicket hauls and a best return of 5-34. For a bowler whose rise was built largely on raw pace, domestic cricket has provided an opportunity to sharpen his control and build the capacity to bowl longer spells. Haris, who emerged from Pakistan’s tape-ball circuit before earning recognition through Lahore Qalandars’ development programme, made his international debut in 2020. “Domestic cricket is just as important as international cricket,” he said. “You go there and work on your mistakes. I tried to bowl longer spells, and having played four-day cricket, I feel that one-day cricket is not as difficult for me now. Your control over line and length improves.” The stint has also prompted Haris to reiterate his willingness to return to Test cricket, a format that became the centre of a dispute between him and the then chief selector Wahab Riaz in late 2023. Haris withdrew from Pakistan’s tour of Australia after initially being considered for selection, citing concerns over workload and fitness. Wahab said the team had planned to use him as an impact bowler in short spells and maintained that the management had received assurances about his availability. The disagreement escalated in February 2024, when the PCB terminated Haris’ central contract, citing his refusal to tour. Haris said he had not been ready for the demands of Test cricket at the time but was now working towards making himself available if Pakistan needed him. “I am looking at myself for that role as well. If the team needs a fast bowler or someone who can provide pace, why should I not make myself available?” he said. “If I get the opportunity to play red-ball cricket for Pakistan, I will certainly take it.” For now, his immediate task remains helping Pakistan sustain their early momentum in the tri-series – in two matches of which he has bagged four wickets at 20 – while addressing a weakness that has persisted across formats and campaigns. Haris insisted that criticism over runs conceded would not deter him, arguing that the demands of modern cricket meant even the best bowlers could have difficult days. “Pace is very important. I work on my fitness and try to maintain it during the off-season,” he said. “I have managed to maintain my pace, and I will continue trying to do so.” With the 2027 World Cup approaching, Pakistan’s challenge will be to ensure that pace, reverse swing and improved preparation translate into the breakthroughs that matter most. For Haris, that begins with taking wickets when the opposition is building an innings, rather than waiting for the death overs to turn the contest.

items.title: Trump’s threat to strike Iran raises public concerns, congressional questions
items.description: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump has renewed his threat of military action against Iran, raising questions about public support for the war and Congress’s ability to restrain further escalation . With midterm elections approaching on November 3, polls show widespread dissatisfaction with the war , particularly over rising fuel prices and the risk to American troops. Reports of renewed US-Israeli military planning have also raised concerns about possible strikes after the elections. Trump made his latest threat at a rally in Florida on Friday. “We may do another little Epic Fury ,” he said, referring to the US military operation against Iran. He gave no details about when another operation might begin. The remarks followed an ABC News report on Thursday that the US military and the Israel Defence Forces had drawn up options for renewed joint strikes. The report cited two Israeli sources familiar with the plans, who said the strikes would most likely take place after the midterms. White House spokesperson Anna Kelly, however, told ABC News that “the United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections.” The reports indicate that further military action is being considered, but they do not establish that Trump has ordered an attack. Negotiations remain another possibility. Strategic choices and political pressure In an analysis published on October 23, James M. Lindsay, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, outlined three options for Trump: escalate the conflict, negotiate with Tehran or maintain the current position. “All three options have substantial downsides and a questionable likelihood of succeeding,” Lindsay wrote. Further attacks could increase pressure on Iran but might prolong the conflict without securing a political settlement. Negotiations would require the two sides to bridge their differences, while maintaining the current position could leave the conflict unresolved. Andrew Payne, research director for Europe, Russia and the Americas at Chatham House, argued in an October 15 analysis that foreign policy could play an unusual role in this year’s midterm elections. The war’s economic consequences could influence voters who might otherwise focus primarily on domestic issues, particularly the cost of living. Public opinion turns against the war A Pew Research Centre survey conducted from September 28 to October 4 among 5,062 US adults found that 65 per cent disapproved of Trump’s handling of the military action against Iran, while 33pc approved. The survey also found that 73pc were extremely or very concerned about higher fuel prices, and 71pc about American troops being wounded or killed. Nearly half, 47pc, expected the military action to continue for more than another year. A separate Associated Press -NORC poll published on October 22 found that roughly seven in 10 registered voters wanted the next Congress to make ending the Iran war a top priority. About eight in 10 gave similar priority to reducing the cost of living. The poll surveyed 1,119 US adults from October 8 to 12. The findings point to pressure on the administration to address the war’s duration and economic consequences. However, dissatisfaction with Trump’s handling of the conflict does not necessarily mean that voters would oppose every possible military operation. Can Congress restrain Trump? Congress can scrutinise military operations, hold oversight hearings and use its control over federal spending to influence the course of the war. Lawmakers can also invoke the War Powers Resolution to challenge military action. The resolution requires the president to notify Congress in certain circumstances when US forces enter hostilities. It also establishes procedures for lawmakers to consider whether military action should continue. Funding could become particularly important if the conflict expands. Congress can approve, restrict or condition spending for military operations, potentially increasing the political cost of a prolonged campaign. The extent of congressional pressure would depend partly on whether Republicans remain united behind Trump. If some Republican lawmakers join Democrats in challenging the war, the administration could face greater scrutiny of its objectives and plans for ending the conflict. Even a congressional challenge, however, would not automatically prevent the president from ordering another strike. The question after November 3 The immediate question is whether Trump will maintain his stated position against attacking Iran before the midterms. The larger issue is whether the election results will alter the political constraints on his decisions. The reported military planning and Trump’s latest remarks keep the prospect of renewed strikes alive, but neither establishes that an attack has been scheduled. A change in control of either chamber of Congress could affect oversight and funding debates, although it would not automatically prevent further military action. Whether the combined pressures of public dissatisfaction, economic concerns and congressional scrutiny lead Trump towards negotiations or renewed strikes remains unclear.

items.title: Pakistan denounces ‘heinous’ church attack in Jordan, reiterates condemnation of terrorism
items.description: Pakistan has strongly condemned the “heinous terrorist attack” on a funeral procession at a church in Jordan’s Karak Governorate, reiterating its condemnation of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. Gunmen killed at least seven people and wounded dozens at a church in southern Jordan on Friday. According to reports, the assailants stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak Governorate and opened fire. According to a statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO), Pakistan extended its heartfelt condolences to the government and people of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, particularly the bereaved families, and expressed its wishes for the speedy recovery of those injured. “Pakistan stands in firm solidarity with the brotherly people of Jordan in their fight against terrorism, and reiterates its strongest condemnation of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations”, the statement added. The incident occurred when gunmen got out of a vehicle and opened fire during a funeral procession, Jordan’s Public Security Directorate said in a statement, adding that a manhunt was under way for the perpetrators. “The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation,” King Abdullah II said in a post on X. “We will strike with an iron fist against those who dare to threaten our nation.” According to images from state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka , the king arrived in Karak on Friday evening. After authorities gave a death toll of six, Director of Public Security Major General Abdullah Al-Maaytah said it had risen to seven with 34 injured, 27 of whom were still receiving treatment. Footage aired by Al-Mamlaka showed two gunmen dressed in casual clothes and brandishing pistols, with a third carrying a long gun as they opened fire on the church. A witness said the gunmen fired continuously for five minutes before fleeing. Between 150 and 200 people were in and around the church at the time, the witness said.

items.title: Circulation nocturne : Près de 400 motocyclistes interpellés pour défaut de casque à Ouagadougou
items.description: La Direction régionale de la police nationale du Kadiogo a intensifié les contrôles nocturnes du port du casque, ce 23 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, dans le cadre de l’opération « Bouclier tête durcie », portant sur la répression du défaut du casque. En trois heures, près de 400 usagers ont été interpellés dans la ville. Au carrefour du Rond-point des Nations unies, 34 motocyclistes ont été interpellés entre 18 h et 19 h 50 pour défaut de port du casque ou port non conforme. Au carrefour du Moogho Naaba, 26 usagers ont été concernés. Ils étaient 54 au carrefour de l’ASECNA et 37 à celui de Total Gounghin. Ces chiffres concernent quatre carrefours visités par la mission sur les 19 annoncés pour cette sortie. Pour Abdoulaziz Yonli, Directeur régional de la Police nationale du Kadiogo, cette opération répond au constat que malgré que le port du casque soit devenu plus fréquent en journée, les comportements changent à la tombée de la nuit, surtout dans les quartiers périphériques. « Les accidents ne préviennent pas. Les accidents ne choisissent pas de survenir dans la journée et de ne pas survenir la nuit. Les accidents peuvent survenir à tout moment » , a-t-il rappelé. Le Directeur régional souligne également que l’obscurité réduit la visibilité des usagers et que les phares peuvent éblouir les conducteurs. Il estime que les accidents nocturnes peuvent être particulièrement graves, d’où la nécessité de maintenir le port du casque à toute heure et quelle que soit la distance à parcourir. « Nous n’avons pas deux têtes, nous n’avons qu’une seule tête, nous n’avons qu’une seule vie. Et protéger sa vie en portant le casque, c’est d’abord protéger sa famille » , a insisté Abdoulaziz Yonli. Il rappelle qu’un accident peut également priver une famille d’un soutien et entraîner une perte pour la collectivité. « Je partais juste à côté » : des oublis qui se répètent-©Faso7 Parmi les personnes interpellées figure Ousmane Kaboré, vendeur de téléphones. Contrôlé au carrefour du Rond-point des Nations Unies, il explique avoir oublié son casque après avoir fermé sa boutique et s’être arrêté à une station-service. Reconnaissant son erreur, il salue l’action des policiers. « Je suis très conscient ce soir que c’est pour sensibiliser la population, la jeunesse. […] Le port du casque, c’est pour la santé de tout le monde» , a-t-il déclaré, avant de résumer le message de l’opération : « Mon casque, ma vie. » Au carrefour de l’ASECNA, Abdoulaye Kodia a lui aussi été interpellé. Il était sorti acheter de l’eau, avec une casquette sur la tête, après avoir oublié son casque à la maison. Il affirme avoir compris la raison du contrôle lorsque le policier lui a signalé son infraction. Pour le Directeur régional de la police nationale, ces explications reviennent régulièrement lors des contrôles. « La réponse est la même partout : “J’ai oublié mon casque ”, ou bien “ je partais juste à côté ”, ou bien “ je partais à la pharmacie, je n’avais pas l’esprit tranquille ”. C’est toujours la même chose », a-t-il relevé. Il insiste sur le fait qu’aucun déplacement ne justifie de se passer de cet équipement de protection. « Que vous partiez à la pharmacie ou que vous partiez à côté, il faut porter le casque. Ceux qui partent même à la pharmacie doivent avoir à l’esprit qu’ils doivent porter le casque, pour ne pas aller à la pharmacie deux fois. Pour aller à la pharmacie, faire un accident et être encore victime parce qu’on voulait sauver une vie », a-t-il lancé. La police appelle à maintenir les bons réflexes-©Faso7 Selon Abdoulaziz Yonli, les contrôles menés sur l’ensemble du dispositif ont permis d’estimer à près de 400 le nombre d’usagers interpellés en trois heures dans la ville de Ouagadougou. Ce bilan ne comprend pas les communes rattachées ni les zones périphériques situées en dehors du périmètre concerné. Le responsable déplore notamment que certains motocyclistes portent le casque pour se rendre au centre-ville, puis l’enlèvent une fois de retour dans leur quartier. D’autres le suspendent au guidon ou le posent sur la tête sans l’attacher correctement. La police nationale appelle ainsi les usagers à faire du port du casque un réflexe permanent, de jour comme de nuit, y compris pour les trajets de proximité. Elle invite également les responsables d’associations et les acteurs de la sécurité routière à poursuivre les actions de sensibilisation. « Que je puisse inculquer ça à mes enfants, que je puisse les amener eux-mêmes à m’interpeller lorsque je ne porte pas le casque et à moi aussi de les interpeller lorsqu’ils ne portent pas le casque » , a exhorté Abdoulaziz Yonli. L’opération « Bouclier tête durcie » se poursuit dans un contexte où la police entend faire respecter le port obligatoire du casque sur les engins à deux et trois roues. Au-delà des contrôles et des interpellations, l’enjeu reste d’ancrer durablement ce geste de protection dans les habitudes des usagers. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article Circulation nocturne : Près de 400 motocyclistes interpellés pour défaut de casque à Ouagadougou est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Fire breaks out at Hitler's mountain retreat, suspect detained: police
items.description: German police said Saturday they had detained a suspect following a fire at Adolf Hitler’s mountain retreat, known as the Eagle’s Nest, in the state of Bavaria. Around 200 firefighters were deployed to tackle the blaze at the Nazi dictator’s remote Kehlsteinhaus residence, on the peak of Obersalzberg in southern Germany. Firefighters saw flames rising high into the air as they approached the scene, only to find the building “completely ablaze”, police said. “A suspicious person was taken into temporary custody,” they said in a later statement, adding that nobody was injured in the blaze. Police spokeswoman Lisa Maier said firefighters struggled to tackle the blaze due to its location at an altitude of 1,834 metres. The building was only accessible with “heavy breathing apparatus”, she said. Authorities were alerted to the fire on Friday evening, when a smoke detector triggered a fire alarm at around 9:50pm (1950 GMT), police said. “The criminal police investigation is ongoing,” Maier added. German tabloid Bild reported that the authorities arrested a motorcyclist they came across on their way to the scene and that they suspected the fire was the result of arson. Built in the 1930s, the Eagle’s Nest forms part of the toxic legacy of Germany’s bitter 20th-century history.
